label: Locus 7200
description: Burial located south of pit 7199 in the western quadrant of the trench. Contains skeleton of a single individual (child) and is poorly preserved/highly disturbed. Burial is inside an ovoid pit that is lined on the north, east, and south sides respectively by a single mud brick, whose level of preservation are medium to poor. The burial was excavated with metal dental picks and small brushes. Articulation was especially difficult as the bones would flake and/or desintegrate upon light brushing. What was determined was that the burial contained a skull with intact teeth, part of the spinal column vertebrae, and what is perhaps the rib bones. The lower section of the individual was either not interned or was not preserved. The teeth were collected in a separate foil envelope. The rest of the bones were in such a fragmentary state that they were lumped into a "miscellaneous bones" envelope. Both bone bags were labeled under one KT (KT1). The entire locus was screened using an 1/8 inch sieve. Any bone collected from this screening was included within the "miscellaneous bone" envelope. No grave goods were found. poorly sorted, angular sandy matrix

description: This is a E-W mudbrick wall collapse.  Initially, we believed that this was a wall abutting/bonded with wall 2029 and mudbrick collapse 2020. The north or south section of the wall never revealed lines either, nor did the west baulk.  After pedestaling the locus for a while, I finally closed it when we regretfully hacked it all down because it was not a wall.

label: Locus 159
description: Ashy layer of fill in north corner of trench. Originally a part of L156; it became apparent that this was very different material and a softer consistency, thus we made it its own locus. Very few small finds, mostly lithics. It is ashy and different enough throughout the locus for it to legitimately be its own locus.The dividing line between this locus and L156, L163, L164, and L166 is not clearmeaining that material classified as belonging to one locus could actually belong to another. This is something to keep in mind when looking at this locus. These loci are producing similar enough finds that it does not make much of a difference. The locus was ashy near the top, and as we uncovered more it lost most of its ashyness, but did stay softer and very different than the abutting series of surfaces.  The finds that came out of it lead us to believe it was definitely not a surface. Any trace of it disappeared into L170. Ashier context than the surrounding loci, especially near its top; softer than the surrounding soil from other loci.

We also took a soil sample from the base of L1008 that contains the ashy soil at the top of L1009.  We took this sample when we found individual charred seeds.  A carbon sample from L1008 KT 1037, also came from the top bit of the ash that  became L1009. We found figurine KT1039 at the base of L1008 but it came out of the ashy soil that is L1009.  This locus seems to represent a rich layer of occupational debris from living contexts.   We closed the locus and the sounding at the end of the season without reaching the end of the soil layer or virgin soil.  The trench was back filled.  A plastic bottle was left at the base of the trench to alert future excavators to the previous excavation level.

It was very well preserved in large sections, but on its edges it was poorly preserved.  The surface produced a lot of pottery and bone, and some interesting pieces of lithic, as well as ground stones, all of which were unfortunately discarded before they could be saved.  Lots of carbon was also found within the surface.  It was a very interesting surface, bordered by the wall L157, L162, the ashy fill L167, and L159, all of which continue down past the end of this locus.  It was a very good context not very far below the last surface.  When excavating it, it seemed as though there were more surfaces directly beneath it, meaning that we could have unintentionally taken out more surfaces and fill than this one locus. These are all the same locus, however, unless/until they become very different during excavation. In the end the ashy corner became its own locus, 159, and the northwest corner became its own locus as well, L162. The dividing line between this locus and L159 is not clear, meaning that material classified as belonging to one locus could actually belong to the other. This is something to consider when looking at either loci. Additionally, these loci are similar enough that it does not make much of a diffeerence. Upon the closing of the locus, a surface consisting of smooth stones was found that spread throughout most of the locus. description: L4007 is the ashy surface inside the clay brick wall of the oven in L4009.  This layer contains a high concentration of splintered/burnt bone, shells, and some pottery.  We also found many small finds including a stone tool and some spindle whirls.  We came upon a harder clay/ash mixed layer and changed locus to L4012. the bulk of the ash from the oven is this locus

label: Locus 58
description: This is a large pit filled with animal bone and pottery sherds. There is alot of bone, mostly large animal. This was likely a garbage dump.

label: Locus 37
description: L37 is a pebble and potsherd surface below the hard clayey loam in L33.  This is a surface similar to the ones in L30 and L32.  This is the best preserved surface of the three and it does not extend all the way to the east baulk but stops abruptly at L36.  We found a lot of lithics, blades and obsidian.  We also took two microanalysis samples and the rest of the surface was separated into artifact bags and screened 1/1.  After we cleaned off the surface we closed L37 and opened L40 as fill below the surface. this surface is stamped into the compacted clayey fill and is uniform throughout

label: Locus 4061
description: The surface next to the East baulk and West of the wall L4030.  A lot of pottery sitting on also some diagnostics.  It has the same kind of slope of the wall.  Sloping down to the North.  Associated with the wall L4030 but doesn"t continue to North (possibly because of the animal holes)

label: Locus 2027
description: Area of plaster patches noted in L2022.  The patches were not extensive enough to be followed or a clear surface level determined, so their immediate area was excavated and the surface was visible in the S baulk.

label: Locus 5044
description: Fill beneath surface L5027 and adjoining areas.  Soft, mixed fill mostly of compressed soil and collapsed mudbrick with some areas of ashy or sand/silt deposists not large enough to make into their own loci.

label: Locus 157
description:
This locus is a pot holder, located SE of L145 and approximately 0.5m west of the east trench baulk. its surface is lined with bright orange-pink pot sherds and mud, forming a concave shape depression. Max. depth: 0.12m

THE FOLLOWING DESCRIPTION SHOULD BE ENTERED IN THE LOCUS FEATURE DESCRIPTION FORM, HOWEVER, SYSTEM RETURNS ERROR:
This feature is a pit filled with small pot sherds (bright orange in color, some burnt), pebbles, and packed with dirt.  A single bone is recovered from the fill.  A fragment of a ground stone was collected from the surface (top of the pot stand). Lithic debitage present also. round, concave pit filled with small pottery sherds, ash, and dirt, some small rocks

label: Locus 4068
description: Baulk cleaning of the southern baulk

label: Locus 4001
description: L4001 is a closed sub floor surface.  There is a lot of dark ash spots, burnt clay, and splintered bone fragments.  One large pot was found in situ directly on top of this layer in L4000.  We think its a closed surface because the stratigraphy in the north baulk wall indicated that there may have been an oven layer with very hard clay/brick which would have protected this layer, thus preserving the context.  At the bottom of this locus we found a lot of light gray ash which continues from the adjoining locus 4005 surface. because of the burnt clay and ash directly about this layer  and the hardness of the soil we believe this is a closed subfloor fill which is a good context

label: Locus 7157
description: Located in the southeast corner of the trench north of fill 7151. Originally designated as a mud brick wall, now considered fill. <3 mm thick whiteplaster-like layer on the west end as possible surface though extremely fragmentary. Pottery sherd scatter recovered on May 30, 2005 on eastern end. Two grinder fragments in secondary disposal context also within this sherd scatter. poorly sorted, angular

label: Locus 1012
description: This Locus is the line of rocks surrounding the burial pit (Locus 1011)

label: Locus 3013
description: This is a cobble stone surface compsed of small stones with some flat lying pottery fragments inside.

label: Locus 42
description: L42 is a compacted clayey fill with surface stamped into it below L40 fill.  This surface is very similar to L37, the surface on top of L40 and the previous surface L32.  The surface appears to slope northward, and is composed of small colorful river pebbles, animal bone and lithics.  Because we have not been able to excavate it we cannot tell exactly what kind of finds are in the surface.  The surface remains in situ. this fill is very compacted clayey fill with a surface of colored pebbles, pottery, bone, and lithics imbedded in it.  This surface is identical to the previous surfaces L32, L37 but a little larger than the two

label: Locus 1007
description: L1007 is fill  south of the rock surfaces. About 5cm down at the south baulk close to the west baulk we encountered a mudbrick-like area that was densely packed and different from the rest of the area.  There were two colors to the area, at the baulk the soil was dark gray, and then it abruptly became lighter with orange/clayish colored areas inside it.  We chopped there it. immediately south of the rock surface, one part of the south baulk had dark grayish soil which stopped abruptly then went to a hard packed area with orange clay colored areas

label: Locus 2004
description: This locus was opened to make sure that the area to the inside of the line of stones L 2003 did not contain anything associated with that structure. this locus has far fewer rocks and potsherds than L 2002 immediately to the north.

label: Locus 2
description: General fill level with a darker soil than level above. As we have found in area F most of these layers closer to the surface have little pottery very likely due to mechanized plowing techniques which removed a lot of the larger fragments. The darker color indicates age of the soil and increased amount of decayed organic material. General fill, a little darker than layer above. Pottery does not account for much.

label: Locus 25
description:
L25 is the large  middle south chamber (of 5) of furnace L2 / L20. Large thick pottery sherds line the West wall/floor of this chamber ( L20 ). And a mudbrick lies across this chamber with slag flowing around and under it.
We finished excavating this when we found the slanted pottery on top of the L20 /27.

label: Locus 7005
description: This locus is a surface made up of a mixture of cobblestones that range in diameter from 5-10 cms. and small pebbles.

label: Locus 59
description: mudbrick wall, 1 clearly visible course with 3 bricks, possibly slump from stone wall foundation L53

label: Locus 7136
description: This locus is located to the northeast side of the L7126. I think that it is an oven; we are not sure yet needs to be investigated in the field season of 2005.

label: Locus 8025
description: Fill excavated as different locus due to color change observed within the pit 8023. Except for a small quantity of pebbles, this level is fairly devoid of rocks and it seems that we are finding less and less pottery color change to a darker soil, absence of white pebbles or reddish soil

label: Locus 1005
description: Originally, Bradley and I thought that the previous locus might be a floor--However, it is quite possible that this locus and the preceeding locus (maybe the proceeding locus) might be part of a greater flood plane of the Tigris.

label: Locus 15
description: The top of this locus was a very compact silty soil.  It is the 1x2 meters in the south half of the trench.  It is equal to L14 which is very similar except the soil there is less compact.

label: Locus 2181
description: Fill locus of sounding

label: Locus 3030
description: oven feature which is quadrilatiraly shaped. The northern part is cut off by 3024. This is the wall of the oven. It has many animal burrows in it. It was founded on and cut into wall 3037. 3027 was one of the surfaces that this oven was used on semi baked mudbrick

label: Locus 20
description:
This locus was opened because between L16 and L18 there was a wall so there sould be two different surfaces. The east of this wall  was L18 and it was changed as L20.
Today is the last day of the excavation so this locus is closed.

label: Locus 8009
description: A THIRD CIRCULAR ROCK FORMATION COMPRISED OF 16 STONES AND ONE PIECE OF POTTERY, THE ROCKS IN THIS CASE ARE SMALLER AND PACKED TIGHTLY. TWO NOTABLE DIFFERENCES WITH OTHER FORMATIONS ARE 1) NO ROCKS ARE COVERING THE NORTHWEST SIDE OF IT, IS EMPTY OF ROCKS. 2) THERE ARE NO FLOOR ROCKS TO THE FORMATION. THIS MAKES ME THINK THAT IT WAS CRUDELY MADE OR PERHAPS IN A HURRY. THE ROCKS USED ON THIS ONE ARE MUCH SMALLER .04 - .07 METERS IN DIAMETER WITH ONLY  FEW LARGER ONES. CIRCULAR ROCK FORMATION

label: Locus 56
description:
L56 is the area of relatively empty fill to the west of surface L37 (under the S end of L8). The east part of this  locus was directly under wall L10.And its boundary with L37 aligns with the boundary of L17 to L10.    


Not excavated in 2002.

label: Locus 4001
description: This locus is sub top soil.

label: Locus 4037
description: this locus is a line of rocks that jets out of the SE corner and travels along the southern baulk.  It may be associated with L4038, another rock line just west, and possibly the goat skelaton at a lower elevation just west.  This locus has only 8 rocks.

label: Locus 7077
description: THIS LOCUS IS FILL/SURFACE POSSIBLE ASSOCIATED WITH STRUCTURE 7053.  IT IS LOCATED IN THE CENTRAL EASTERN PART OF THE TRENCH.  IF THE WALLS OF L7053 EXTEND EASTWARD, THIS WOULD BE AN INTERIOR FILL.  AS OF 7/25 IT IS AN ARBITRARY LOCUS.  THE WALLS DID NOT EXTEND - IT IS AN ARBITRARY LOCUS

label: Locus 2137
description: Cleaning and staigthening of the south baulk, an area that could not be drawn unless cut back.

label: Locus 27
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V

label: Locus 52
description: This locus goes from topsoil on the eastern edge to almost a meter deep in the west balk. The locus encompases the entire trench. exceptionaly rocky. Rock size ranging from pebbles (less than 5cm) to one larger 30cm

label: Locus 5016
description: Mudbrick collapse atop surface level L5028

label: Locus 7047
description: This locus is comprised of cobbles, pebbles and soil.  It appears to be a  possible new surface or part of a surface L7005.  This was given a context rating as secondary due to the fact that it was exposed to the off-season elements.  It was an irregular surface that produced a lot of lithics/pottery/bone and had a pit underneath.

label: Locus 2098
description: Feature in the southwest corner of the trench bounded on the north by a white plaster line.

label: Locus 1062
description: Under the ashy pit which I took KT1489 from yesterday is more soft dirt.  We will try to dig the extents. There was ash here and so the soil has black, very silty parts

label: Locus 7
description:
This locus is opened because when we were digging L4 (the north-east part of the trench) we found a skeleton pieces so we gave this locus to this area. To see the skeleton clearly the north baulk of the trench was widened 0.5m through the north and it was widened 2.1m through the west from the east baulk. I forget to give a new locus number to the burial so L7 contains the burial and aroun it. 
Skeleton appeared to be lying in a flexed position on its right side, with the head facing east. Burial definitely detached at waist and no other bones were in sight.
Today is the last day of the excavation so this locus is closed.

label: Locus 4057
description: This locus is below L4052. The south part of the old pit.

label: Locus 1
description: First locus given to entire trench for the removal of the surface soil. Excepft finds, artifcats are not kept since this is the developed soil. Soil was not moist when this description was made.

label: Locus 6
description: This locus was thought to be a reddish fill similar to locus 3. However it is part of wall locus 5 and is equivalent to it.

label: Locus 23
description: This is a wall. This wall was the south border of floor L9.

label: Locus 5128
description: SE oven in and attached to S mudbrick house. located in the far southeatern corner of the trench.  This locus is the foundations thereof.

label: Locus 19
description: Sub-fill below wall L14 and above lower architecture.

label: Locus 16
description: This locus consists of three rocks which seem to running from northeast to southwest, but the rocks might be wasah materila too.

label: Locus 128
description: remaning fill above the L118 surface. the same material as L107 and 108.

label: Locus 2038
description: L2038 is a mudbrick configuration to the east of L2037. It appears to be associated with L2037.

label: Locus 2069
description: Black ashy layer around pot in pit coimpacted black ashy soil

label: Locus 7198
description: Subwall fill below 7154 in the northwest corner of the trench. Cut on the southern end by pit 7162. Contains mud brick debris and is highly compacted. poorly sorted, angular

label: Locus 1091
description: This is a pit just to the east of the unexcavated stair.

label: Locus 1026
description: The pit appeared as the North section of the trench, 1023, was being leveled of. It was very soft, fine ash , under which a harder surface, that slopes downward, from N, downwards to S. end. very loose and soft, deeper at the S-end.

label: Locus 17
description: L17 is compacted fill below the wall in L7 equal to L14 because of the similar mix of mudbrick, ash and clay and the proximity of the two loci as seen in the south and west baulk.  We changed to L17 because after much scraping and discussion we decided the wall could not have been founded on an ash layer located directly below this layer as L18.  We found no bricks in this section and we also realized that the wall did not reach the east baulk so we took off the fill underneath the wall as L17 and the fill adjacent to the east end of the wall which was identical fill. this locus is fill compacted beneath a mudbrick wall on top of an ashy fill

label: Locus 1101
description:
This is a cobble surface that we have uncovered in between several large rocks.  The working hypothesis is that this is actually probably wall slump and that this is not a cobble surface but the cobbles were part of a wall which has collapsed over the years along with the big rocks forming another part of the wall.  

This was not excavated this season.  Have a great time with it next year though, whoever takes over this trench.

label: Locus 4
description: Lots of white pebbles are located within this fill, may be a virgin soil but many of the pebbles look more like fragments of chalk rock. Rocks in the corner began appearing at 570.78 and were detailed but not separated by locus number. Light color soil with white pebbles interpersed within it

label: Locus 1017
description: seems to be a burial pit, loose soil was filled, found some human bones, but it was disturbed, probably from being under the large rocks.  The locus should be extended after removing these large rocks (Locus 1016) and look to see if there is any relationship

label: Locus 4011
description: It is the contuntion of the surface, with the L4009. But I decided to make it my path way that me and my workers can work easily.

label: Locus 1127
description: This locus is located east of fill L1127 and directly south of L1124 in the southeast corner of the trench. Deep animal burrow in left center area of locus.

label: Locus 1039
description: begun as a locus right near the baulk.  maybe a wall or other barrier, as the color of the dirt here is a brown, which contrasts with the much darker black and grey ashy layer which abuts it.

label: Locus 49
description:
L49 was first thought to be  the foundation trench for wall  L10, found just S of L20 cutting surface L17.
Upon laterinspection (after removal of L10).no difference could be seen between this and the surface under L10 and the locus was expended from 15cm wide to 25cm, to include the area beneath 10. This fill seems to be intentimally placed. and is very similar to fill L52 and 8.

label: Locus 3097
description: This locus was created for pottery collected during the cleaning of the east baulk from off season wash  in the year 2002- none of the locus description information above is reflecting actual data.

label: Locus 3
description: Subsoil

label: Locus 4122
description: This locus is the second of two defined loci from the baulk extension to D4.  We decided to make the distinction between 4121 and 4122, because we saw more collapse like content (burnt mud brick and ash) in 4121.

label: Locus 81
description: It is NW corner of the trench and behind the locus 79 mudbrick wall.

label: Locus 4007
description: This locus is very smilar tot he last locus.  We are digging in arbitrary levels, hence the locus change.

label: Locus 2046
description: Fill under bricky area of 2038

label: Locus 4028
description: Although the trench was covered during the offseason, we excavated several 5-10 cm cleaning loci to be sure no contaminated material remained. The loci generally correspond to the various different elevations of soil left from the previous season.  This locus is from the south-central portion of the trench.  There was one large rock (50cm x 25cm) that sat on the border of L4031 and L4028.  It didn"t seem to be associated with any feature.

label: Locus 3042
description: Pit filled with ash and little pottery. Part of the top was collected in 3024. Bounded on north east by a small group of rocks. We origionally thought this was a round pit but the boundry changed when we found it was square and included 3029 Ash is compact when dug and sloughs off into abgular slated but crumbkes into very powdery, chalky feeling ash when crushed in hand. No bone or stone only pottery. Homogenous.

label: Locus 200
description: This locus is the new wall that runs from the southeastern corner of the trench to the northwest corner. This wall forms a cell that runs into the eastern baulk. It was not excavaed before the end of the season.

label: Locus 3005
description: We dug this area to see if we could detect the possible floor  we found at the bottom of L. 3003. And after this it was extended to cover the entire trench. This fill might be the tumble on top of a floor

label: Locus 36
description: This locus was distinguished from the overlying locus 32 because of the emergence of the reed surface 30 to the west. Otherwise it is virtually indistinguishable from 32, a semi-compact reddish fill.

label: Locus 1007
description: Most of the rocks are no larger than 5 x 5 cm.

label: Locus 3
description: This fill layer was uncovered beneath subtopsoil locus 2 in the north-eastern corner of the trench and consists of a reddish compact soil with mudbrick debris. The locus ends with the appearance of a mudbrick alignment to the west running north-south. Ceramics and other materials are not abundant in this locus.

label: Locus 2026
description: Area west of mudbricks 2013.  Designated a separate locus due to the presence of the wall stub/collapse, L2023. It was only fill and no surface was found.  It ended when the wall stub was removed.  It was combined with L-2025 to make L-2037.

label: Locus 8
description:
This is just a fill. no seeable features.
It  is in Northern half of the trench.

label: Locus 1061
description:
This area acted as a mini sounding to find out more about the area next to the pit and to see if the rocks went further than the bottom of the pit.  The rocks did not.  The soil did get more dark and ashy near the end of this locus, so we decided to change loci when we dug this part again. 

Ended up continuing this locus as a hard packed fill area once the ash pit was defined as a separate locus.  Stayed as a locus for over one month but finally ended with everything being brought down to level.  Some debate as to whether this locus actually ended up as a wall next to the cobble surface, which is part of the reason we closed the locus and started a new locus

label: Locus 32
description: This fill underlies the white reed surrface 21 and consists primarily of a semi-compact red-brown fill. The locus was terminated with the emergence of wall 33

label: Locus 7
description: All information cataloged under locus 8

label: Locus 183
description: Locus 183 is a fill locus to the west of Locus 182 in the southwest portion of the trench. It represents the fill below wall Locus 170.

label: Locus 80
description: It is a free area between door way L75 and cobble wall L78. It looks like L77.

label: Locus 9038
description: This pit contained a lot of bone and many cutting stones.

label: Locus 5229
description: This is the new locus given to the sounding in the SW corner of the trench Description was made when the soil was too moist.

label: Locus 32
description: This locus was first thought to be a pit, but after starting to excavate the locus it turned out to be clean that it was a wall like feature before, but what I hve revealed seems to be chewed up now, and now we are only able to observe a few burned mud- brick slabs.

label: Locus 3050
description: Fill layer of oven 3030 beneath the ash layer breaks into ashy silt and rounded clay bits

label: Locus 3059
description: This is mudbrick collapse from a nearby wall probably inside the baulk. Continuation of L3049. This is a small amount of collapse, probably just accumulation not direct collapse. This is mudbrick

label: Locus 7218
description: Small pit in the southeast corner of the trench. Lined internally by ring of pot sherds of various wares and fabrics. Sandy pebble matrix with residual sherds and a grinding stone fragment are located directly in the center of the pit. With the removal of the sherd lining, a thin burnt plastered interior on the western and south sides was uncovered. 5cm pebbles were found on the basal level of the pit. Locus was excavated with a screening ratio of 1:1. high rate of compaction, angular to subangular sand matrix

label: Locus 142
description: Locus 142 is a fill locus running north-south between Wall Locus 131 and the eastern baulk of the trench. It is bordered in the north by Wall Locus 139.

label: Locus 21
description: An area of muddy red/brown fill

label: Locus 7150
description: Burial located along southern edge and within fill L7145 and cutting mud brick wall 7160. Heavily damaged, most probably from initial pick axe excavation of this area but mostly due to poor preservation.  Long bones were found tightly packed together along with ribs suggesting a crouched or flexed positioning of the body. Exact orientation or articulation of the individual was unavailable.

label: Locus 4079
description: Because of the slope of the tell the eastern edge of trench D4 is still very close to ground surface. This locus is a thin long excavation unit that is at the far eastern edge of the trench. The purpose of this locus is to remove the mixed fill from this endge of the trench.

label: Locus 7
description: CONTINUATION OF THE MASSIVE COLLAPSED BRICK ENCOUNTERED EARLIER. THIS, AS EXPLAINED BEFORE MAY BE CONSIDERED ONE WITH LOCUS 5 AND 7. INTERESTINGLY NO POTTERY WAS LOCATED.

label: Locus 4049
description: This locus is the same as L4042.  We named it as a separate locus because we excavated the rocks above this locus (4038)  after L4042.  However, it would normally have been included with L4042.

label: Locus 2009
description: L 2009 is the area of fill in the western trench below the level of the soil change observed on 8/8/2000. It was closed when a layer of very loose, pit-like soil was discovered.

label: Locus 4060
description: NOT EXCAVATED during Year 2001;  The feature in the North side of L4041.  Scattered rocks with pottery.  There are possibly more than one course of rocks (?)  It is possible this may turn to a surface because there were a lot of pottery and also one long piece of pottery lying on these rocks.  But the rocks are not compact , mostly not touching each other.

label: Locus 7155
description: Located in the northwest corner of the trench. This locus was opened as the fill area west of wall 7154 and has since been partially replaced by 7163, 7164, 7162, and 7161. poorly sorted, angular to subangular

label: Locus 4039
description: This locus is a rock pile near the center of the trench.  I can not tell whether or not it is associated with any of th eother stone features in the trench.  it is, however, at a similar elevation.

label: Locus 5002
description: Rock feature including one possibly worked stone with a groove and some pock marks.

label: Locus 1
description: Removal of topsoil.  All artifacts found were discarded as poor context.

label: Locus 1103
description: Stone wall previously called L1069

label: Locus 11
description: Unexcavated as of the end of the season.  It is the area below the burial pit.

label: Locus 1005
description: While leveling the trench with L.1002/1003, we came upon a wall, L1008, and changed all the loci around and on top of the wall.  The fill on top of the wall is L. 1005. We found the same mix of artifacts in the fill, as in the earlier layers. The soil seems to be same as 1004, plus (maybe) a little mudbrick debris.

label: Locus 155
description: This locus is the wall foundations that were uncovered during the last season.  We took out the walls until it was at the level of the surrounding surfaces.  These walls had so badly eroded that no bricks were visible upon removal, and the top of the foundations were eroded and mixed with topsoil, so not much could be learned about the bricks of the walls.  Once removed, though, it revealed many bricks, indicating the walls continue even farther down and were thus likely earlier than the surrounding surfaces.  With this particular locus there is no locus description because these walls were so eroded and yielded no relevant information. Sticky

label: Locus 103
description: Locus 103 is located in the NE corner of the trench, where it is 1.6 m wide. It tapers off into the west baulk of the trench 4.3 m from the NE corner. The soil is darker and slightly more compact in Locus 103. It borders the street (Locus 102), however it does not appear to contain any architecture.

label: Locus 47
description: L47 is the rocks and pottery grouping at the north end of L8 (nowto L20 ).It consists at mained rocks from 8-18cm which extend in an arc from the NW corner at L20 out to the N and W, stopping at the N or thenboundary at L48.

label: Locus 4090
description: off season wash in western half of entire trench mixed silt clayey soil washed in from off season

label: Locus 190
description: Locus 190 is a subfloor surface in the room in the northern portion of the eastern baulk extension. It was initially thought that the surface represented an associated subfloor with the room, but the surface is clearly below the walls meaning it probably represents an earlier outdoor worksurface

label: Locus 5000
description: removal of the baulk between D1&D2 topsoil level

label: Locus 4009
description: Bits of charcoal found while extending (deepening) the L4008 extension of the A4 trench.  Just beneath the charcoal and adobe bits were a scatter of potsherds, one large chert cobble with several flake scars, and the ball of a femur.  All were assigned to this same locus.  7/30/2001 Took color of lower fill and got 10 YR 5/2 (Andrew Ugan).  Original color taken by Amy Stevens.

label: Locus 29
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V

label: Locus 4021
description: (Previously Level 8) mudbricky soil w/ ashy layers and burnt clay.  We found a complete pot in the NW corner of the section.

label: Locus 4
description: An area in the NW composed of mudbrick debris/fill - context unclear

label: Locus 2036
description: L2036 is a pit on the east baulk north side.  Characterized by loose mixed soil.  Soil is reddish brown mixed with light colored ashy soil.

label: Locus 11
description: This was designated as a new locus as it appears to be an oven sitting on the surface Locus 10. Its characteristics give the idea that it is an oven. Red and brown dirt is observed mixed with shades of black and gray. Unfortunately there is no visible burned parts. There are pieces of burnt pottery or better yet pars of the oven wall. There is also quite a bit of small calcaneous pebbles white and soft. These pebbles look almost like lime or chalk. There is also some potery in association with the oven one a fragment of a pitcher like container which appears to be chalcolithic has a small spout still in one piece

label: Locus 5129
description: Shallow area in WNW under plaster-lined pit L5085 but above any surface feature. Origin of fill unclear.

label: Locus 2101
description: Pit of dark ash to north of wall 2088.  Soil and carbon samples were taken. very ashy, powdery, dark carbon rich fill

label: Locus 4034
description:
This is a burial which is also located at the south end of the L4000 test trench.  Not identified last year.  Showed up while brushing out the trench.  Lies oriented E-W just south of and slightly above 4029 burial.  Clearly an adult or older sub-adult (large).

This locus equals locus 4031, which was fill identified east of the initial skeletal material and which originatied higher than the skeleton as initially viewed coming out in 4028.

label: Locus 11
description:
On the East baulk of the trench there are some brick sections and plaster lines so it may be a wall to understand this we wanted to dig east part of east baulk (2x2m) so this locus was opened as top soil.
This locus was closed because after digging this area we arrived different kind of texture (silt loam) so this locus number was changed as L12. top soil

label: Locus 2129
description: part of enormous wall system at south end of trench; continuation on west end of 2126. mudbrick bands alternate color in section as well as in plan; probably part of terrace or retention system or city wall. part of enormous wall system at south end of trench

label: Locus 37
description: This locus is the debris or fill accumilated directly on the wall 33. It is composed of a brownish semi-loose fill. It was distinguished because of the appearance of the wall and was used to achieve tighter control over the stratigraphy.

label: Locus 7061
description: This locus was opened for cleaning of the southern baulk.  This was to be able to collect the material separately.  Cengis did not realize this was separate from the Eastern baulk and used the same KT bags from 7060 for the material from this locus as well.

label: Locus 4134
description: Orange surface under collapse. While we changed loci at this color change, we actually dug through this surface thinking that it was to soft and silty to actually be the floor.  We later decided that this was the floor and it was actually just incredibly burned.

label: Locus 31
description: This locus belongs to the locus that is located to the south east of the previous pit L13.

label: Locus 5
description:
This locus opened because this area was the south part of the stones area, L3, and it had different structure than L3.
This locus was closed because after taking cobble stones off there were not any different structure between L5 and soil beneath L3 and the middle-east part of L1.

This locus was opened because there were cobble stones as different than the other locus.

description:

However, the ongoing excavations in this part of the trench showed that at least the very NW portion of the wall continues further down. The east side of it is unclear due to the mixture of mud from L.5207 and animal burrows.
Brick size is not clear in each case but the first ones in the west are: 70x50x10(?) cm.
This locus is open because its bottom until the depth of 586.10 m. has not been confirmed this season.

label: Locus 1089
description:
This is a surface, and a pretty nice one at that.  Seems to be a surface contemporary with the cobble pathway 1086.  There may also be a wall (1096) which we think may keep the surface inside or outside.

As we came right down upon the surface in the locus above it (1083) we were able to find three nice examples of blades, one obsidian and two chert.  These were finds in L1083, although they were probably laying right upon this surface or just above it.

In the middle of the trench, but in the far S part of this locus we have a jar coming up which we think may be a complete large storage jar which was buried in the surface 1089.  That would be awesome to see this jar.  Jar actually appears to be related to this surface, or the even better surface just below it L1098.

It must be said that this surface locus is nowhere near as good or cool as the surface which it capped, L1098.  Look to there for the cool surface stuff of this context.

There were multiple pieces of grindstone in the pile.  It was closed when all the rocks were removed.

An impressive spider shot of the entire trench was taken before the final destruction of the Wonder Pavement.

This confirmed that the red color was due to the mud area being heated repeatedly--slowly and poorly fired.  It was closed when the entire red area was removed. It could be the residue from the heat of an oven.  We have found ash in the vicinity in the surrounding locus.

label: Locus 166
description: This is the fill/sub-floor beneath the surface that was L164. It border the north side of the wall and goes to the north corner stopping at the circualr locus that is L159. The border between it and L159 is unclear meaning that either locus could have bags contaminated with material from the other. It consists mainly of soil mixed with rocks, lithic, bone, and pottery. We were unable to munsell it because we were waiting for the second pick pass to occur with it, having assumed in the beginning that the locus continued.  Once removed, however, we realized that the now revealed surface was indeed a different locus.  Thus we missed the opportunity to munsell.  This locus revealed an ashy soil in the southeast corner of the locus, an increased area for L159, and a new surface consisting of stones, pebbles, and many flat-lying pottery sherds.  Thus this locus was a fill of 8-10cm between two different floor surfaces.  The ashy soil in the southeast corner was present from the beginning of the excavation of the locus, but was not made into its own locus, L167, until after L166 had finished.  We wanted to wait and see if it really was different.  This means that several of the artifacts from L166 will truly belong to L167, but since these two loci are so closely interconnected it is acceptable for this to happen.  These two loci only touch as far as we can see; there is no indication that L167 was a pit cut into L166.

Closed again when we thought the pit layers were removed.  This was again  proved wrong by the line in the section when we opened L-2033 in the same area. Little pottery or bone coming out of this pit.

label: Locus 154
description: Locus 154 is a fill locus spanning the majority of the trench. It contains everything except a one and a half meter portion along the northern baulk.

label: Locus 54
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V

description:
HAP sample of floor L66
total floor volume is 36 L -  not including HAP

label: Locus 5030
description: Fill below surface L5025.  Soft soil w/ many bones

label: Locus 5
description: Continuation of the fill from locus 2, contains the same small white roots

label: Locus 4040
description: This locus is a rock wall (part of) or possibly just a rock pile that sits just south of L4034, the pit where we found the burial.  The rocks are just above the elevation where we found the human remains.  I can"t say that the two are associated with each other.  There are about 16 rocks that form this locus.

label: Locus 5007
description: Area of fill at southern extent of mudbrick wall L5008, in area beneath a pit excavated in D1. Generally soft soil

label: Locus 2030
description: This is the area north of wall L-2029 bordered on the west by collapse L-2020.  It was fill, but we did encounter an area which seemed to be oven residue.  It was bagged as KT 2251/2252.  No good surface was found, but there is a hard area abutting L-2029 which we thought was a wider lower course of the wall that could be part of a floor.  The locus was closed when it was taken down level with the remains of L-2020 and L-2032.  It became L-2040 which was closed due to the end of the season.

label: Locus 1086
description: This is a pit visible on the norhtern side after 2001 excavations, but clearly visible on all sides after removal of L1085. mudbrick cap iwth dirt followed by more mudbrick.  Large rodent and root disturbances.

label: Locus 2069
description: small shallow ash pit associated with hearth 2073

label: Locus 7103
description: This is the pit which is sitting at the North east portion of the trench since 2002. The side walls of the pit are yieling a stratigraphy to us.

label: Locus 114
description: Locus 114 is a fill locus coverning the western half of the trench. It is cut on its eastern edge by the street in Locus 113, and abuts the Ubaid wall in Locus 108.

label: Locus 115
description: pit. kidney bean shaped. filled with mudbrick debris -- from L114/116? -- including two bricks that seem to be from when this wall was blownout. ash deposibt -- burnt grain -- and burnt residue along the northern edge. L114/116 continues at the bottom of the pit. pit enlarged to an oval on 6/19

label: Locus 29
description: There are no KT bags from this locus too.

label: Locus 1012
description: the continuing of the L1011 separated into 2 loci, this one,s major purpose was to isolate the L1013( the cobble stones), we could have succeeded in this act , towards the corners soil becomes aa little harder. North and south sides of the cobble stone area

label: Locus 2146
description: pebble surface underlying cobble pavement (2143) north of wall foundation 2139; abuts mudbrick support underlying wall foundation 2139 pocket of 8-10cm cobbles and a flat lying pot sherd with fingernail impressions near west baulk (see photo); also more 8cm cobbles towards southern part of locus

label: Locus 7014
description: This locus is a group of small cobblestones and pebbles in the southwest corner of the trench.  It has an interesting shape as the north end of the feature is at the same elevation as L7019 but then rises 15 cms. to create a lump in this area of the trench.The large lump is composed of sand...Hmm... 7014 grew to include a hint of a surface, but was reduced to the original "lump" before final excavation.  A large amount of pottery was found interspersed with the stones in the lump.

label: Locus 20
description: The soil in the small trench changed color t a lighter shade locus # was changed. We are going fast to get to the cobbles and perhaps the wall L 6 and L 2. White pebbles began appearing

label: Locus 2064
description: Plaster-lined wall in NW corner of trench.  Part of the same structure as 2050. Not excavated in 2005.

label: Locus 2032
description: Fill in northwest section of the trench.  It abutted two mud brick collapses, L2020 (to the East) & L2013 (to the south). During its excavation a mud brick wall, which can be seen in the north baulk, was destroyed.  It had some hard areas, but the collapse it abutted always seemed more dense and hard than anything contained in the locus.  It was finally closed when the mudbrick on both sides was razed.  The area under those walls and fill was then changed to a new locus.  Two nice mixed together potsmashes were found, but no concrete surface. Two large potsmashes.  A surface could appear imminently.

label: Locus 4093
description:
This locus is a row of rocks located in the central western portion of the trench. This locus is an other wall foundation that might have a connection with L4081; the connection between L4093 and L4081 is done by a conglamate (a big rock that is being formed by some pebbels).

[The east side of the wall has been taken out.]

label: Locus 14
description: This is a wall. Not just a single piece of straight wall this is a corner of a structure. It is located in the NE corner of the trench. There is a small step down from the western half to the eastern half. this step is the result of the way that the trench was excavated and is not a natural feature of the wall. The sample piece of mudbrick had a large piece of pottery in it, this may not be representative of al the pieces.

label: Locus 1030
description: North of wall L1011, there is a roundish pile of medium rocks.  Possible collapse from L1011, but also quite round.

label: Locus 7134
description: This locus is consistines the stones that are on L7126.

label: Locus 5036
description: Oven.  Circular.  Some pottery lining.  Probably contemporary with similar features L5033 and L5048.

label: Locus 187
description: This locus is the southern wall of the cell that is in the northwest corner of the trench. It is different from the rest of the cell because it is below the other walls of the trench and there was not a clear connection to the other walls. These bricks, once L157 was removed above it, were extremely shallow and took only a little scraping to make them completely disappear. This s possibly why they do not have a visible connection - some bricks were completely removed during the removal of wall L157 and are no longer present. We think this wall is the bottom of L157, but since it goes just as deep as the structure below L157, we believe that it"s a part of the earlier structure and was later added on to.

label: Locus 7083
description: This locus is an arbitrary fill locus assigned after the grid system was removed.  It is located in the NE quadrant and consists of soil, some random pebbles and potsherds.

label: Locus 4014
description: the fill between L 4011, 4012, 4013 in the NE portion. Opened arbitrarily because of the new strata.

label: Locus 3015
description: Alignment of rocks in a square with a circular pit at its NE end. West of the circular pit is a slag/conglomerate distribution, Conglomerate seems to be formed by contact of  flows. This could happen if once molten slag or by eroded conglomerate

label: Locus 8002
description: THIS IS A SMALL OVEN LOCATED ON THE WEST WALL OF THE TRENCH AND I WILL GUESS AT THIS TIME WAS PLACED THERE AFTER A HOLE WAS DUG. THE WALLS OF IT ARE ON THE TRENCH SIDE AND ARE BROKEN BUT POSSIBLY HALF OF IT REMAINS AT LOWER LEVELS. ONE BAG OF CONTENTS FROM WITHIN THE PIT WERE RECOVERED FOR FLOTATION. WILL SIFT THE REMAINING PART OF THE CONTENTS AS WE GO DOWN.  A SECOND BAG OF CONTENTS WAS REMOVED FOR FLOTATION FROM A DEEPER LEVEL. TRYING TO FIND FLOOR IN ASSOCIATION. SMALL PIT LOCATED INTO THE WEST BAULK MADE FROM ROUGH BAKED CLAY.

label: Locus 2
description: THIS LOCUS DESIGNATES THE COBBLE STONE SURFACE LOCATED SHORTLY AFTER BEGINNING EXCAVATING TODAY. THE SURFACE ADVANCES THROUGH ABOUT ONE HALF OF THE TRENCH. IT IS A BAND OF TIGHTLY PACKED STONE WITH SOME REDDISH SOIL FILL PACKED IN BETWEEN. DEPTHS VARY 3 TO 10 COBBLE STONES LAID AS A SURFACE. TIGHTLY PACKED WITH VERY LITTLE POTTERY

label: Locus 1022
description: Extension of the burial 1015.  Seems to have a loose soil that extend further West from the pit 1015.

label: Locus 171
description: Locus 171 is a burnt surface emerging out of the west baulk in the center of the trench. Our initial though was that it represented an outdoor work surface associated with wall Locus 159, however no connection could be confirmed. Upon removal it probably represented an oven or a fire place given the presence of a rock and potsherd foundation at the bottom of the locus running into the western baulk.

label: Locus 23
description:
Locus 23  is the fill surrounding the South wall of furnace (L2/L20).We created this locus to isolate the material directly adjacent to the furnace for later analysis.(see L21).The theory being that mud / clay would be packed against the side at the furnace to insolate and support / protect it.
On july 15 we cut a 15cm section out and comes across a large stone.then moved directly west and tried again .We found a change to soft soil 12cm deep.
Upon removal of L20 we noted brick lines in the remaining buttress of L23.

label: Locus 7108
description: This is the area which began to show up two seasons ago and was thought to be an area where a pit way show up.

label: Locus 20
description: Cobblestone foundations of wall L17.  Continued from the east where they were first discovered in trench F19. Exposed only in the NE end of the trench and in trench F19.  Not removed. 15-25cm diameter cobblestones running roughly NE-SW.

label: Locus 4067
description: Not Excavated in the Year 2001 season.  The fill on the East side of the walls L4064 and L4062.  Also on the west side of L4030.  Separated because of the location of the walls.

label: Locus 5047
description: Deep pit in NW corner of trench with areas extending beneath the entire area of a later occupation (L5034, 5037, 5039)

label: Locus 7066
description: This locus was opened when a different in color and texture was apparent after removing 7056.  The locus is a small pit that held mysterious material (maybe organic) and the skeleton of a small bird.

label: Locus 4030
description: Mud brick fill.  Substantially harder than nearby 4031 fill.  Appears under locus 4020.  Depth unknown at present.  May have extended to the west, but was removed when Locus 4000 trench first dug.  Locus identified mostly by its sharp contrast with the softer L4031 fill to the north.  Initial exposure measures 50 by 50cm.  This was subsequently expanded to include a 50cm wide (approx) strip running E-W along the southern margin of the southeastern 4x2m block of A4. 4030 has a much higher density of mudbrick type fill and tends to be harder and more difficult to dig.

label: Locus 1130
description: This locus is located in the southeast corner of the trench. Silty pit with ring of ash inclusion on its outer edge. High levels of ash and carbon inside with subdivisions evident in east and south baulk. It is highly probable that this locus is the outer edge of the Chalcolithic oven excavated in F4.

label: Locus 3008
description: (Previously Level 5) This locus is a surface.  There are two lines of large rocks lining, parallel to N-S (slightly tilted to East).  In between them small rocks are placed (rocks of 10 cm or less ).  Also, in North part of the surface is pebbled layer.  Several flat-laying sherds were found.  Some compacted mud is exposed.  This could be a pathway, or a steps leading towards the top of the hill.

label: Locus 5157
description: Excavated as a feature in 2002. A section and an examination of the east baulk suggested that both the baulk and the section in the wall itself revealed limited evidence of mudbrick construction. However, the presence of reed impressions and the consistency of the soil composition lead to the conclusion that this had been excavated as a standing wall when in fact it was more likely to have been the continuation of the mudbrick etc fill shown in locus 5167. removed and the area reclassified as 5167 and 5174 cleaning loci for fill.

label: Locus 129
description: Locus 129 is a charred surface in the northwest corner of the trench that could represent an oven or other burned surface.

label: Locus 143
description: This locus is located in the south eastern corner of the trench. It is composed of fill which yeilds lithic debitage, bone, stone implements, and pottery sherds. A large storage, painted Ubaid vessel was recovered, partially contained within the south baulk. locus filled with brown dirt, yields cultural debitage

label: Locus 13
description: This locus is a floor. This floor was visible in the balk and is above L9. When straighteneing the balks enought was preserved of this surface to designate it as its own loci.

label: Locus 8013
description: THIS IS THE GENERAL FILL BELOW COBBLESTONES WHICH I CALLED L8012 THAT WAS HOPED WAS A SEALED SURFACE. THE CONTENTS WERE CAREFULLY PROCESSED FOR BONE, CERAMIC, AND LITHICS. LOCUS WAS OPENED AND CLOSED TODAY. FILL CONTENTS JUST BELOW COBBLESTONES

label: Locus 1074
description:
This is a fire installation.  Floatation sample taken.  Location is just in front of the two possible entrance stones of locus 1075.  A second surface appeared directly in front of the stones, between the stones and the fire installation.  This area will be a separate locus.  Excavation has been postponed until the wall loci (1075, 1077, and 1069) have been removed and a greater area at that level can be investigated.
Cut into 1075, possibly or built over. burnt

label: Locus 3019
description: This is a fill laye that may contain some very incoherent, lightly used work surfaces riddled by animal burrows

label: Locus 32
description: This is a fill beyond the mud wall (L35)

label: Locus 2122
description: possible wall oriented east-west, or possible burial marker. oriented east -  west

label: Locus 1044
description: This is the fill level underneath the clay surface 1040 on which the brick pavement was placed.  This area came out in large clumps, but analysis confirmed that it was only fill and not bricks which we were cutting into. the area seemed to come out in large clumps and boulders, although the dirt seemed to be general fill once the dirt was broken.

label: Locus 9
description:
We wanted to dig the south-east part of L1 to see is there any wall or surface. After digging this part 15-18 cm we arrived the different kind of texture (silt loam) so this locus was opened.
This locus was closed because after digging L9 approximately 30 cm we arrived a different texture (compact loam) so this locus was changed as L10.

label: Locus 3037
description: This is a N-S running wall of stone. In places it has cut pieces of conglomerate in place of stones at some points has a cut piece of conglomerate in its structure

label: Locus 5098
description: Grain floor in central-W.  Currently identified as some a grain of some sort, but exact identification remains elusive.  Connects all the Ubaid loci by abutting and stacking up against walls L5140 and 5141, oven L5138 and connecting to hard surface L5132

label: Locus 128
description: Locus 128 is a fill locus situated between the emerging walls of Locus 125 and Locus 117.

label: Locus 4037
description: Virgin soil.  No artifacts.  This locus had a huge step cut out of it so the elevations are very different.

label: Locus 9007
description: This is the fake virgin soil to the south of the hard clay L 9003.  It is the same soil as L 9001, but as it was separated by the hard area I made it a new locus.  It was about the huge organic ash layer L 9006.

label: Locus 49
description: This locus appears to be the deliberate intermittent deposition of ash from either an oven, or successive use and occupation of a living surface. Blackened ash layers are interspersed with brownish fill layers clearly visible in the section. The locus was excavated by peeling off the layers one by one. Very good sample of diagnostic pottery, carbon, ashy soil and a small find. This is an important locus!

label: Locus 17
description: This is the final locus in this sounding.  it is a sterile, sandy, rocky soil that was naturally deposited.  No artifacts were found...

label: Locus 1071
description: arbitrary locus division for control purposes.  Is equal to other fill locus L1070.  Fill.

label: Locus 136
description: Locus 136 is a fill locus bordering on the south baulk of the trench. The soil here is lighter than the remainder of the fill in the trench, and could suggest a mixing of middle bronze and Ubaid contexts.

label: Locus 7038
description: This locus is a subfloor fill located directly beneath surface L7024.

label: Locus 4
description: This locus is a burial represented by a skull that we partially chipped/smashed while digging Locus 3 in the northern end of the trench.  The skull is an adult but we cannot determine sex from the small exposure.  The top of the head is up and the back of the head is to the NW, suggesting that the burial runs NW-SE or N-S in orientation. We do not plan to excavate this burial because the goal of G8 is to ground-truth the geomag data.

label: Locus 6
description: The locus is East of the trench.Subsoil.

label: Locus 4035
description: the oven occured in the Sw quarter of the trench. At the top level that we found the oven the walls were not complete. But in the lower level it is. Also we found some greenish organic material in it. A little part seemed to be collapsed in becaue we found some clay reddish ditr in it. This oven was different than the other ones. Because the walls were a lot thinner and also very loose that while we were taking the walls off they were getting broke from the middle into two. As there was vry high  temperature inside that destroyed the walls. Note that we found that slag pits in this area and strata.

label: Locus 22
description:
This is a fill in the SW side of the wall (L 21), which is posiibly inside of this wall. W side: 8.80 m
E side: 6.70 m

label: Locus 2007
description: A mud floor which meets the rocks in L-2003.  It appears to end toward the north end of the locus.  It is isolated to the eastern side of the trench.  We saved the floor to float, but closed it when we hacked through it.  The floor was extremely hard and the soil above popped off quite easily.

label: Locus 4111
description: This locus is the actual collapse from the wall L4110.  It was covered with a thick layer of ashy fill (L4109). This layer was primarily composed of large burnt mud bricks with ashy fill in between the collapse. Composed of burnt mud brick of varying colors.  Dimensions: H=10cm, L=42cm, w=25cm

label: Locus 1021
description: We decided that the rocks in the North of locus 1012 is different.  So we separated the North half to be locus 1021.  The rocks in the South are still 1012.

label: Locus 5069
description: Very hard soil surface of western room of mudbrick house.  Has a slope from S-N downhill, and plaster layers above (L5068).  Virtually no cultural artifacts.  Closed at end of season.

label: Locus 1067
description: thin ashy layer.  fill locus L1065, maybe pit, appeared to end at this point.  May continue or grow larger, or may actually be a separate pit itself.  Actually was a very thin layer.

label: Locus 4008
description: I thought that it was the plow zone, but I recognized that it is the contution of the L4009.

label: Locus 151
description: This locus lies beneath the layer of mixed stone and pottery (possibly surfaces).  The soil is very mixed and contains lots of pebbles and artifacts.  The excavated area represents the edge of the ancient tepe.  We didn"t fully excavate the northern half of this locus.  At the bottom of the western half, last year"s EB and LC wall is visible.  This suggests that good contexts are preserved beneath this level.

label: Locus 18
period_label: Middle Bronze Age / Early Bronze Age

label: Locus 4091
description: This locus is located in the northwestern portion of the trench. It appears to be a area of mud brick collapse between 4090 and 4089. We are not sure if this is collapse from the stone features 4090 and 4089.

label: Locus 2000
description: steep incline with thin (1-2 cm) top dirt w/light ground vegetation soil of consistent texture and color. Topsoil all the way down the step trench. dirt containing several small pebbles, tree roots causing difference in compacticity of soil but with no notable changes in hardness.

label: Locus 20
description:
Ashy soil - extension of L8 oven discovered after removal of L 10 in the E.
Also includes the W extension under the baulk and into D5 (July 20, 2004).

label: Locus 18
description: it is located under the loc11 and west part of the Trench.(PIT) soft and ashey soil.the colour darker and burnt

label: Locus 1010
description: We stopped digging 1007 in this area, because the soil seemed looser, therefore thinking it was a pit. But as we excavated the "pit", it became clear that was nothing, and we closed it.

label: Locus 8021
description: SEALED CONTENTS BELOW SEVERAL LOCI. Fill in between cobble surfaces and new locus 8024, for collection control purposes. believe this fill to be the same under all cobble surfaces collection below all cobble areas

label: Locus 28
description: The fill inside  North chamber (of 5) of furnace L2/L20. Narrow chamber without much slag.

label: Locus 135
description: Locus 135 is an Ubaid fill locus in the southern portion of the trench, just south of wall 131.

label: Locus 5032
description: Excavation of questionable area of southern SW-NE wall L5008.  Mostly mudbrick collapse above surface L5027

label: Locus 79
description: mudbrick wall beneath floor L78, difficult to tell whether it is wider to the south (actually extends for another row into L77) and whether mudbricks near pit L74 are related (possibly mudbrick slump), pseudomorph organic residue found with a floor that possibly runs beneath the wall. possibly another row of bricks to the south -- removed accidentally during excavation. evidence for a floor surface when removing extra fill (L91) around the wall (pseudomorphs), but no remains under the wall.

label: Locus 4090
description: This locus is a row of rocks extending in to the west baulk in the middle of the trench. This locus is more or less in L4085. The rocks seem to be sitting on the surface 4085, and I think that this locus runs from the west to the east. I think that these rocks might have a close relationship with L4089.

label: Locus 5230
description: New locus for SW sounding after L.5229.

label: Locus 4050
description: another slag looking place with pebbles close to the W baulk. Looking like L4049. Melted pottery and oven fragments with a burnt melted look.Stuck together in a way that it is hard to pick the little pieces from there. This is also a very tiny locus. slag looking with pottery and pebbles

label: Locus 50
description: this locus consisted of an ash layer and the material -clay loam- above part of it in the eastern half of the trench.  the ash layer slopes down and becomes thinner west to east  we began this locus at the beginning of the ash in the west and found more of it in the east.  float sample was taken when we first found the ash in locus 46.

label: Locus 4068
description: Two rocks were standing here.Next to the old pit,L4028 from last year.

label: Locus 5039
description: Mudbrick wall.  Forms the E edge of surface L5034, at one point probably joined with wall L5037 to form the NE corner of said surface but has since degraded in that area due it downslope position and less protection by topsoil, etc.  Piles of pebbles and pottery accumumlated from floor along the W edge.

label: Locus 3040
description: fill within oven below devep of 1st course of hard mudbrick wall;  Whiter plaster inclusions fill which spreds accross in oven where ash does not cover the presently visible surface. Is hard compact fill dirt which is quite fryable- seems to have bee burned but is also eroded at the top as if it has been exposed to water and then dried slightly bluey grey inclusions, gley 2 6/1 5pb bluish grey. Possible degraded oven wall

label: Locus 4031
description: This area was not dug.  After being scraped and swept it became part of a new locus, L4037, which is bounded on the south by L 4041. Bounded on the south by a red clay line which is part of the locus.  The color disappears in the east, but the soil texture is still the same and markedly different from the loose, chunky soil to the south, so I extended the locus boundary.

label: Locus 11
description:
Possible pebble foundation to locus 2 wall stub.  But significantly lower and was dirt fill (possibly brick like material) between loci.  Very hard matrix.  Almost concrete like.  Must break up to remove.

Actually, this was most likely river stone conglomerate.  The stone could have been used as some sort of foundation for the locus 2 wall stub, but was probably just one stone not another sort of surface or feature buildup.

label: Locus 4079
description: the fill on the north east side of the wall L4070. we found carbon samples in this fill

label: Locus 3007
description: (Previously Level 4)

label: Locus 2105
description:
This is a cleaning locus, cleaning the wall labeled L2117. 
See 2104 in connection with the bottom depths one, though in the south end two rows

label: Locus 3
description: New fill level with slightly lighter color than locus 1, it also appears that it is finer in texture than locus 1. One would think that a lighter soil migh contain less organic decomposed material in it. Would dust storms and high winds have contributed to a quick laying and covering of soil layers that prevented or slowed growth. This locus extends throughout the trench and so it would appear to have been fairly evenly deposited during a time. Erosion deposition

label: Locus 2128
description: ash layer situated directly below 2116, which is a layer of loose fill soil dessicated from the winter off-season. L2116 contained lots of occupational debris indicative of a courtyard or kitchen-like cooking area. locus does not extend all the way to wall 2125; peters out before abutting wall 2125

label: Locus 1031
description: Possible pit in Northeast corner near rocks.  Lithics are very prevalent here, many pebbles. This is defined in the corner by the large rocks of L1026 + L1036.  There were a lot of pebbles and very good lithics.

label: Locus 3011
description: Locus 3011 is initially defined as an area of loose, brownish-grey soil associated with L3009/L3010 burials approximately 75cm below ground surface in the south side of the L3000 trench, west end.  It is similar in color and consistency to the silty loam forming L3000 generally and may be identical with it.  It is somewhat similar to L3013 sediments to the west, but distinct from the hardened mixed adobe melt and ash of 3015 to the north. Fine silty loam consistent with L3000 and containing burials.

label: Locus 78
description:
low density pebbled surface. possibly lying between walls L70 and 72. street surface associated with Chalco sherds. HAP sammple taken and all sifted. articulated and cleaned on 6/1
149 L total surface - not including HAP

label: Locus 8001
description: GENERAL FILL TYPE SOIL, PERHAPS CONTAINING MORE MOISTURE THAN SOIL ABOVE. THIS LOCUS IS CONTAINED WITHIN SAME SIZE TRENCH 5X10 METERS NORTH TO SOUTH SOIL COLOR IS DARKER THAN L8000 IT APPEARS TO BE MORE COMPACTED THAN SOIL ABOVE. SUB TOP SOIL LAYER.

label: Locus 7119
description: This locus is located at the interior pait of L7118 where the reddish brown mud-brick is running West-East.

label: Locus 3
description: compacted clay matrix with <3.0cm small rocks. Charcoal deposit in NW corner from pit (as identified in north and west baulk profile)

label: Locus 1015
description: mud brick wall possibly burned. (Because of the colors) Reddish mud-brick, some of them are black and there are white specs in between. But the wall in a bad situation so it is impossible to know the rows, courses or the sizes of the mud-bricks

label: Locus 2050
description: Wash layer exposed to open air during season.  Does not correspond to loci used in previous year.  Locus reflects current observation of surface.  Note that it includes an area previously designated as a "wall" possibly in locus L2046 which has subsequently been robbed of its stone. This locus is itself multi-lay (mixed):animal holes; erosion; dense-ish clayey soil under soil under which runs a sandy fine .5 to 1 cm layer of dark brown material with pebbles and gravel of underlying surface adhering

label: Locus 123
description:
This lucus in located in the center of the trench within the central cell of the Ubaid house. It consists of two rows on mud bricks that probably made up the bottom or floor of the cell.
Last year this locus was 141 but was assigned 123 at the beginning of the 2007 season after the trench was cleaned. two rows of bricks inside a cell in the Ubaid house

label: Locus 205
description: This locus is in the southwestern corner of the trench, in the trench extension. It contained L191 and has not produced many finds.

label: Locus 5077
description: Area of fill slightly different to L5070 as the sounding went down and thus left in situ.  Unexcavated.

label: Locus 7023
description: This locus is another layer of pottery debris that was found in the central area of the eastern half of the trench. It was located directly beneath L7018.  It was one of many debris layers found over surface 7030. * Put meter stick in slightly different area

label: Locus 5003
description: L5003 is a linear alignement of rocks running essentially north-south about 4m west in L5000 test trench.  The south end of the alignment abuts the L3002 burial and may be cut/truncated by it.  Most of the rock is river rolled, but there are a few pieces of vasicular basalt which may be ground in places.  7/25/2001  Took a closer look at the vasicular basalt (VB) pieces.  Although all three are smoothed (wind or water?), none appears to be deliberately ground.  Need to wash and look at piece in lab to be definite about it. label: Locus 6
description: This locus is the pit containing two burials.  Individual one (I1) was interred in an extended position, head west and feet east, with the legs bent at the knees and sitting up and to the north.  Individual one was distrubed when Individual two (I2) was interred.  I1"s right arm and head were displaced, but the rest of the body was found properly articulated.  The disturbed parts of I1 were placed over it"s neck and I2 was laid over I1"s head in a bundle.  That is, I2 seems to have been interred secondarily in a pile of disarticulated bones.  It is difficult to say which cranium belongs to I1 and I2.  They were found back to back, facing opposite directions, both slighly off center of their proper position at the top of I1"s neck.  My sense tells me that I1"s head is the one facing SE and I2"s head faces NE.  I assume this because what I believe to be I1"s left arm was found under I1"s displaced skull.  It seems likely that the displaced bones, head and left arm, were set there and then I2"s body added.  Also noteworthy is the absence of all but a single piece of a mandible.  Fully 1.5 mandibles are missing fromthis burial.  They either went missing when the southern baulk of F1 was cut and eroded in previous seasons. Or, more likely, I2"s mandible was not interred at all because it was a secondary burial, and I1"s mandible was disturbed when digging a pit for I2.  Thus only part of I1"s mandible made it back into the pit.  Finally, I1"s skull had the first cervical vertebra stuck to the base of the crania by dirt.  This finding is more in keeping with the primary, articulated condition of I1, versus I2, which feels secondary and if so is not likely to have its vertebra preserved.  The metal pin was found near the pelvis of I1 but a a higher level, suggesting that it is disturbed from its original position but I still feel that it belongs to I1 because it was not associated with the bones of I2.
