Actual living surface itself on which the activities related with those finds and the hearth is NOT found in the excavations.

label: Locus 2015
description: Small pit area lined with pot sherds and rocks.  It did not extend far and was contained entirely within L-2014.  It appears to be another reddish burned area associated with an oven.  Perhaps some sort of installation for one.  It was closed when the pottery, rocks and discolored soil were removed. Shallow like L-2004.  Probably more oven residue.  The pot sherds lined the outer circle of the burned area.

label: Locus 4038
description: This is an area of fill, somewhat pitted with softer areas.  It had a couple of small ash deposits, but these were not pits or features.  The soil had only minimal artifacts, but its presence forced us to keep digging because there is some cultural deposition as it is not virgin soil and there was the occassional potsherd.

label: Locus 7130
description: This locus is the locus number of the cooloapse mud- brick pieces which are sitting on L7118 (the interior part of the LC house). The colour of the mud- brick is varying to 2.5 YR 3/3 dark reddish brown.

label: Locus 1083
description: This is the area directly below L1069.  It is a possible mudbrick surface or some other architectural feature that the wall 1069 was built on top of.

label: Locus 4007
description: Found by Hamdallah.  A human crania exposed in L4000 adjacent to the L4008 spur (east trending side trench).

label: Locus 1117
description:
Pebble surface.  Originally thought to be between walls 1111 and 1110.  Now found to extend below wall 1111 and across the western top half of the trench.

Eastern half HAP sampled and screened.  HAP = 18 liters.  Screened total = 261 liters
Western half/under wall 1111 sampled and screened.  HAP = 7 liters.  Screened total = 189 liters

100% of pebble surface removed.

label: Locus 4101
description: this locus which is an ashy pit , on the north of the trench and on the east of the L4099. i found very dark brown burnt soil when i dug in the deep

label: Locus 63
description: ash pit, cuts into floor L66, few artifacts recovered

label: Locus 57
description: It is back of the furnace, some part is mudbrick pieces.

label: Locus 15
description:
L15 is a grouping of rocks (large + small) on the 2nd step, W center.
It consists of bazalt, sand stone and various other rocks intcluding a  "conglomera" pile.We have found this association accross  KT and believe it is associated  w/  metal smelting,and possibly w/  the furction of L2 / L20.
There was very much pottery and small rocks under the large stones with loose soil.

label: Locus 1005
description: very compact reddish clay loam.  possibly some sort of mudbrick feature although no bricks were identified in the section.

label: Locus 88
description: Locus 88 is the fill below house structure in Locus 84. It is located roughly in the center of the trench and runs into the eastern baulk. This locus revealed another street surface in its southern end.

label: Locus 6017
description: Bradley thought that this locus might be a floor.  He originally said this after looking at the North Baulk.  This is further supported by the lack of artifacts in this locus and the fact that we found a lot of artifacts in L6015 (just above). The silt came out in small chunks.

label: Locus 3
description: loose soil in northern 2/3 of trench.  Surface Locus 2 does not continue into this area.  Contained some cobblestones, a few of which were found together at the northern baulk and may be the edge of a surface outside the trench to the north. We found EB pottery throughout this locus, including a pedestaled bowl with finger impressions around the neck.  The soil is reddish brown with white lime bits, like the "virgin" clay found at the base of cultural material in Area F, but is very loose and soft and contains artifacts.  Compare this locus with the F11 and F12 sections not too far to the west.

label: Locus 113
description: pit.  large rock on the top center -- possibly part of wall L119. plastered (?) edge extends downward, possibly a surface, but most likely the edge of the pit. difficult to trace to the southwest.  lots of evidence for organice pseudomorphs (grain storage?). organic pseudomorph also found in this area in locus 77, 100 and 103, and we may have missed the top section of this pit.

label: Locus 54
description: This loci is a bowl placed upside down over a burial of a sub-adult human contained in plaster inside the bowl.

label: Locus 1006
description: moderate to very compact.  As with L1005, very little pottery in this locus.

label: Locus 4120
description: Fill on the North side of Wall 4119.

label: Locus 5191
description: base of the set of loci that equate to the oven. Noted an almost circular line that enclosed this locus that equated with the baulk section. The assumption is that this is a pit onto which the oven has been built. Pottery samples seem to suggest that the pit and the oven are both Early Bronze.

label: Locus 47
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V
description: It is a pebble surface.

label: Locus 1034
description: Associated w/burial (kt 1148, 1149, 1150, 1151).  W/in 5cm of skeleton in all dimensions.

label: Locus 2032
description: Area S of walls 2033/2034

label: Locus 138
description: Locus 138 is an Ubaid fill locus in the center of the trench between wall 117 in the west baulk and wall 131.

label: Locus 9
description: FEW ARTIFACTS

label: Locus 55
description:
group of pots lying on a mud floor. covered with burnt debris. mud floor to the west is burnt. evidence for mudbrick slump and possible corner in the western corner. floor touches wall L43. pots continue into the SW baulk. soil sample taken (3 L)
*order of dates for KT numbers reflects a midseason reorganization

label: Locus 4060
description: This locus is on the north side of the pit excavated as 4048.

label: Locus 2111
description:
This locus is the removal of a wall excavated last year as L2080. Even though the dirt has some of the same feel as mudbrick, it has no definable mortar-lines. So there can be doubt about the solidity of the wall"s claim to of mudbrick, more likely pise.
At the western end of the excavated area, this locus, the soil changed color dramatically to a more reddish/orange color.  
All the material from this locus was sifted, but unfortunuatly the finds where mixed with the not sifted finds.

label: Locus 2055
description: collection of rocks located at 13m peg; oriented east-west with one enormous flagstone at the eastern most end.  Possibly a wall foundation. locus cleaned to dimensions of 2m x 1.8m although the stones which constitute the reason for issuing the locus are only 1.55 x .80m;  stones not organized in neat rows.

label: Locus 7001
description: This locus is located in the majority of the western half of the trench.  It is topsoil that had bushes and some ground cover and was very flat.  it was defined separately from L7000 due to the absence of plow furrows in this area of the trench.  After excavation it was clear that there was no difference between L7000 and L7001.

label: Locus 1081
description: This is the northern half of what was L1075.  It is a surface of mainy squarish cobbles carefully placed.  It has been differentiated from L1075 since that locus appears to be more densely scattered pottery fragments.

label: Locus 3048
description: This is the fill above the oven 3030.

label: Locus 1088
description: This is a pit (or an architectural feature that is pit-shaped) due west of 1086.

label: Locus 9012
description: This locus was under the ash layer in the eastern half of the trench and was cut by the sounding in the north.  The soil became loamier and less ashy so it became this locus, but its 0.50m length is arbitrary.  To understand the trench better I took this 0.50m area and pushed it down  0.50m. A more true brown than the soil above and also different due to the absnce of ash and mudbrick particles.

label: Locus 9034
description: Disregard this Locus - I defined it based on what we thought was a wall and surface but later realized we were not yet to the level of the 2001 season when we unearthed plastic.

label: Locus 196
description: This locus is located in the trench extension on the southern end of the trench. There have been few finds and the soil is very dry and rocky. Wall L200 also runs through this locus.

label: Locus 2009
description: This is a pit.  Soil is a different color from surrounding area.  Small animal bones have surfaced in this area.  It was closed when the parameters of the pit began to change.  This whole area of the trench was filled with pits.  It seemed we had hit on a pit which cut another pit so the locus was changed to L-2018.

label: Locus 1008
description: An arbitrary level that ended when we hit a new type of soil.  Changed locus to 1009 when the soil became ashy and we found lots of pottery as well as a figurine.  When we found the figurine we screened the dirt around it looking for the other half, which was broken in antiquity, but we did not find it.  The figurine actually  belongs to locus 1009 but was found at the bottom of 1008 which pushed into the top of the ashy soil layer. some tiny pebbles less than 1cm

label: Locus 7071
description: THIS LOCUS IS FILL THAT HAS BEEN ARBITRARILY ASSIGNED IN THE SOUTHEAST PART OF THE TRENCH.  IF STRUCTURE 7053 EXTENDS EAST, THIS FILL WOULD BE LOCATED ON THE EXTERIOR. IT IS DESIGNATED AS A PRIMARY LOCUS DUE TO ALL OF THE DEBRIS FOUND WITHIN THE FILL THAT IS PROBABLY ABOVE AN UPCOMING SURFACE

label: Locus 5025
description: N-central rock feature.  Strange surface.  Layer of flat-lying pottery sherds w/ many, many large, core-type lithics but no bones or debitage whatsoever.

label: Locus 152
description: This is a cleaning locus, so it will not produce a lot, if any, KT bags.  It consists of the erosion that has accumulated over the past couple of years.  At its end we will get down past the plastic protection that covers the trench and thus prepare for excavation during this season. This is a preliminary cleaning locus, and thus there is no consistent or relevant color.  It is simply topsoil.

label: Locus 2145
description: This is a surface in the sw corner of the trench, with flatlying stones and pottery. Unfortunuatly not much dirt among the stuff. Will be excavated as L2146

label: Locus 5108
description: ESE area N of large oven in S mudbrick structure.  Created because of uncertainties of associations between the mudbrick house and contexts physically slightly further away.

label: Locus 4049
description: (slag possible) feature with burnt pottery sticked together with some pebbles. Kind of melt. It is clay pieces and burnt oven pieces, some possible ash stuck into it and some pttery all together. At the top level there is no ash, the pottery is bright reddish color  but when we went deeper it changes to a more ashy look. The pottery coming out has a smooth face on one side (bottom). It is very hard as a rock. The rocks in it coming with burnt clay pieces stuck tothem with burnt stuff. the color is varying everywherebut going to an ashy color from bright orangewhen we go  deeper

label: Locus 169
description: This locus is a surface beneath the surface L168, abutting the wall L157.  On its south side is the ashy soil that is L167.  Prior to excavation the surface appeared rocky with many flat-lying potsherds and other artifacts.  The last surface, L168, was separated from it by not more than 8-10cm.  We determined it was a surface once excavation had already begun, having thought it was fill until we were already in it.  There were multiple stones and flat-lying potsherds exposed at the top of it.  These materials were mainly concentrated next to wall L157 and extended out from the wall about 3ft.  It was poorly preserved everywhere else, and at places failed to produce much of this same material.  We took it all together as one locus because there was no clear change anywhere besides the absence of surfacey material and we assumed that at least in some places it was nothing more than poor preservation that caused this.  This locus produced a lot of pottery, bone, and lithic, as well as some carbon and a ceramic figure that is broken off at the end.  At site we could not tell what ths figure was.  It produced this type of material for about 8cm. At this level the soil changed and artifact inclusions lessened.  Probablythe fill between this and L168 was taken out accidently with L168.  Also, this locus seems very much to be apart of a series of outside surfaces pressed very tightly together.  Moreover, it"s level proved to be very irregular and part of its surface was still visible as apart of the fill layer below it, L170.

label: Locus 2154
description: This locus was dug to get a section of the wall L2143. It is located in the northwest quarter of the trench. The other purpose of this locus is to eliminate the two pits L2123 and L2124.

label: Locus 41
description:
line of rocks running EW in the south 1/4 of D6. 3rd step.

Not excavated in 2002. mixed stones and pottery.

label: Locus 108
description: Locus 108 is a wall locus in the northwest corner of the trench that is, most likely, associated with the 2nd millennium pit (Locus 101). The fill below the wall belongs to the Ubaid period based on ceramic finds. The fill is sitting on an emerging surface with collapsed mudbrick fill. Possibly a mudbrick collapse

label: Locus 2080
description: fill context cut by pit 2058; located at 5m peg to the north of wall 2076 base of 2080 is harder packed than the upper part. Medium sized cobbles at east baulk at base of 2080

label: Locus 5152
description: Spatially unchanged from 2002 locus 5116

label: Locus 7201
description: Located in the southwest corner of the trench. Two walls that connect at a corner. North-south running wall has lighter pink bricks than the rest of the locus. The bottom of this wall was not reached in the 2005 season. poorly sorted, angular

label: Locus 1029
description: Wall that appears to be one brick wide, with alternating bricks of about 10 cm long and 26 cm wide.  There are some bricks that appear to be a lighter color, almost white and some that appear to be a darker gray.  The wall actually ended up being only one course.  One theory which I espouse is that this wall may have acted as a curb or enclosure of L1033, the very large pavement, as it was built above the mudbricks, but right at the end of the bricks.

label: Locus 174
description: This locus is within the pit known as L172. It is a burial of a human, most likely a child. It is not contained within anything but is placed directly into the wall, under mudbricks. These bricks could have possibly been placed directly on top of the person after burial. This burial also has mubricks below it, which is most likely an extension of the wall L157. It is in close proximity to the burial found in the last dig season in this trench.

label: Locus 3
description: Fill across entire trench below topsoil and locus 2 cobbstone surface.  Overlies burial L4 in northern part of trench.

label: Locus 2100
description: surface below ash lens layer; indicated by doorpost resting on top elevation of the shift (visible in east baulk) from ash to reddish soil. Located between 5m and 8m pegs

label: Locus 4048
description: This is a sounding we put int the south west corner in an attempt to reach virgin soil.  I changed the KT bags every 25cm or if there was a discernable change in the soil.  It ended at virgin soil.

label: Locus 145
description: This locus was designated due to its color difference from the surrounding loci.  It extends over the SW quadrant of L136.  It can be described as a scatter of baked orange clay, which at places is fused with metal slag.  After excavating the locus, it appears that it is a melted kiln due to overheating. The locus contains large amount of big ceramic vessel(s) sherds. Below the burnt material and ash layer, in the north part of the kiln pit, an area covered with white reed pseudomorph layer was exposed. The bottom of this pit was lined with hard packed mud, underneath which is dirt. area of bright orange clay scatter

label: Locus 2096
description: motley colored medium packed fill layer with ash lenses (2095); above a surface (2100) the transition for which is preserved in the east baulk. Located at the 5-7m peg and south of surface 2049.   east baulk preserves transition from L2096 + L2095 (ash lens fill) to surface 2101 this locus contained lots of lithics materials

label: Locus 2090
description: Pit in the southeast corner of the trench composed of gray ash that appears to continue under 2088.  It may be cut by the continuation of mudbrick wall 2080.

label: Locus 18
description: This is a fill locus. THis locus was taken down in order to clearly define walls L14 and L19. This locus started at the same level as the floor L9 and is now below it. this locus borders L9 on the west side of this locus.

label: Locus 5084
description: Fill below L5078, now certain of lack of off-season contamination.  Possibly a fill above surface, but exact context is unclear.

label: Locus 4044
description: This is an ash pit in the south western corner of the trench.  It extends into the baulks so there is a nice section.  Finding this ash pit is what kept us digging, if only fitfully, in this trench.  Not many artifacts came out of this pit.  Most of it was subsumed when we put in a 1m x 1m sounding in the corner to try and reach virgin soil.  It was closed due to the end of the season.

label: Locus 4107
description: We originally divided L4106, 4107, and 4108 as such thinking that L4108 was a wall.  However, we realized that the whole area was collapsed wall from L4110 and that these three loci should have been defined as one (later defined as L4109). Ashy burn layer over collapsed wall

label: Locus 4059
description: whitish crumbly possible plaster coming out with flat bottoms

label: Locus 2054
description: Probe at 2m peg sunken into wall 2042 (2066) and fill 2053 in order to identity south edge of 2042 (2066). Probe exposed rich occupational levels, including surfaces and a large hearth. A 7cm deep layer of greyish mudbrick (2059) above a burn layer (2065) in the east half of 2054; below that is one layer of hard packed brick material  with charcoal bits dispersed throughout (L2062) abutting another hard packed brick layer (L2063) which i

label: Locus 105
description:
ash pit, ceramic pieces (from oven?) found within the pit along with a few other pottery fragments. crescent shape although it has expanded into circular pit passing into the southeastern baulk, EB pottery
contributes to the mixing of this half of the trench

label: Locus 5225
description: This is the burned plaster surface probably belonged to a hearth found in the S portion of the trench. It was preserved partially and much less than the earlier L.5227 surface below it. It also does not have any edge making impossible to make sure about its size. However, the surface L.5227 below it has the edge preserved in the E and S sides, which might be used as reference for this surface. Thus, this surface might well have the same size surface as the L.5227 below it.

label: Locus 7094
description: THIS LOCUS IS THE INTERIOR ASHY SOIL OF A CIRCULAR FEATURE FOUND IN THE NE QUADRANT OF THE TRENCH.  WE DO NOT KNOW WHAT IT IS EXACTLY.  IT MAY BE A PIT, BUT THE OUTER "WALLS" ARE QUITE WIDE.  THE "WALLS" TO THIS FEATURE IS L7095.  AS OF MY LAST DAY OF EXCAVATION, WE DECIDED NOT TO CLOSE THIS LOCUS.  IT WILL BE LEFT OPEN AND EXCAVATED AFTER I LEAVE.

label: Locus 4005
description: The dirt is starting to come up in very large/dry chunks.  Some of them are as big as 25cm X 25cm.  There is  a small amount of dark ash mixed into this locus. There is a tiny bit of a very black substance, possibly charcoal/dark ash, mixed with the dirt

label: Locus 78
description: It could be a place with cobble walls.

label: Locus 2046
description: potsmash on a surface (2047 + 2048) with associated grindstone. Located at 8m peg at east baulk.

label: Locus 2126
description:
one band of an enormous mudbrick wall;  located  7.5 m peg; reed mat ran in between one pair of courses--most likely used as structural support. Mudbrick wall has alternating colors of green, red, yellowish, grayish, chocolate brown bricks with distinct courses and rows; courses are preserved in east and west baulk as well as south baulk where the other components of the wall extend. note--lower 30cm of 2114 is equal to the wall formed by 2125, 2129, 2126, 2132, 2131. 
note--reed mat 2130 runs in between one pair of brick courses at the east baulk; visible in east baulk as white organic material

label: Locus 85
description: possible floor surface, flat lying pottery and bones, soil sample taken (3L), multiple layers of flat sherds may indicate either multiple surfaces or a single thick fill deposit multiple layers with a few vertical sherds in between

label: Locus 4008
description: 4008 is identical to L4000 but occurs in  the 2x4 meter spur running E-W between 2 and 4 meters north in A4, L4000.

label: Locus 133
description: very loose soil

label: Locus 1085
description: Soil underneath L1075, an ashy layer.  We postulate that the ashy stuff must have come to rest upon a surface and that this would be said surface.  Also appears to go a little farther to the west than the ashy stuff does.  For now excavating as surface under 1075.  This surface is a hard baked clay area.  Also went further down into the fill underneath because with the big pick the soil came out in huge clumps.

label: Locus 3001
description: Topsoil probably by erosion and plowing. Deposited and disturbed Loose eroded dirt with rocks loosely in the soil and many roots.  Also many animal burrows.

label: Locus 197
description: This locus is in the northwest corner of the trench. It is the fill under what was once L173.

label: Locus 56
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V
description: It looks like a oven pit area. A lot of ash soil inside and around that . They used to some mud stuff to arhitech.

label: Locus 131
description: Removal of wall from Ubaid house. Brick walls with various degree of erosion, single course mostly, except wall dividing L124 and L125 is two coarse. this locus consists of all brick walls of the Ubaid house in D8

label: Locus 24
description: This is a layer of fill, most likely part of a fallen wall (L23.)

label: Locus 3029
description: This is a pit that cuts 3018 and we found later that it was part of a larger pit 3042

label: Locus 2024
description: some rocks up to 10 cm

label: Locus 4000
description: L4000 is a initially a 2m wide test trench extending 8m north from A1.  It is defined as all undifferentiated  topsoil and subtopsoil occurring within this area.  It essentially represents the fill in the trench that cannot be assigned to another locus.

label: Locus 14
description: This organic white surface is the second such locus after surface 12. However this surface is fairly ephemeral compared to 12. Again it is very broken and uneven with modest artefact remains. The surface does not continue any further north than locus 12 and seems to follow a comparable spatial plan, which is confined to the southern extremety of the trench. After excavations of the trench were completed it became clear that white organic deposits are to be associated with the wet course construction o mud brick walls.

label: Locus 1001
description: Previously Level 1, This was a poorly excavated trench

label: Locus 15
description: This locus is a north-south wall in the south-west corner of the trench. It is composed of green, red, gray and brown mud bricks. A possible white organic surface, locus 14 may be associated with it.

label: Locus 14
description: L14 is mudbrick debris located south of the wall in L7 starting from the west baulk continuing east about a meter.  It is abutted by L13 which is soft ashy fill.  We opened L14 under L8 because we found a clear division in the east and west halves of the locus between ashy fill and mudbrick debris.  We found a section of mudbrick collapse along the west baulk that had two different colors in it, the south half was red and the north half was a green grey color.  We chopped these down as separate entities and gave them separate KT bags, the red half of the collapse did not produce any artifacs.  Closed the locus when we found more ashy fill a few centimeters below the mudbrick debris, we changed the entire area south of L7 to L13, soft ashy fill. this area is basically mudbrick collapse south fo the wall L7 in west baulk area

label: Locus 10
description: The locus was unexcavated as of the end of the season.  It is the area below the cut L 8.

label: Locus 4027
description: It is the path way that I have left to walk on and to work much easier.

label: Locus 45
description: This is a floor and subfloor locus. The floor was extremely pitted and hard to define we we took out the subfloor with it in some places. Because it could not be well defined neither a soil or HAP sample was taken.

label: Locus 7
description: This locus is a very soft area in the middle of the trench. It may be an ashy pit or surface area.  We did not excavate much of this locus. possibly a pit.

label: Locus 5131
description: Far NW cut into baulk to allow excavation of NW burial L5135.  Wholesale removal of baulk was stopped at this level to allow excavation immediately above the burial to help determine its context.  S portion of this locus appears to still be contained within the large plaster-lined pit of L5085 whereas the N portion is not entirely clear.  Heavily rodent burrowed. passes through various layers

label: Locus 1115
description:
Mud brick area - collapse?  Were smaller bricks inbetween walls 1110 and 1111.  Collapse or surface?

May have some overlap with 1113 fill but separated because of different consistencies.

label: Locus 4082
description: this is cleaning locus for 4074,whice is a fill on the side of wall L4071 . L4074 is the new locus number4042.pieces plaster found on east side of L4082.also some carbon was taken near the east of wall

label: Locus 124
description: Locus 124 is a floor surface of a potential oven or fire collapsed room in the NW corner of the trench. The surface is burned with layers of collapsed mubrick and other debris laying on top of it.

label: Locus 41
description:
This is a circular area with its edge visible in the E side. Its soil has no significant difference than the outisde area of L.38. It dissappeared after excavating it about 10-13 cm. and then became visible again. This shows that when the area is humid it does not show its edge and any color difference or texture from L.38. Slight difference in the soil color and the more or less circular edge only appear after the area receieves several hours of strong sunlight. It is not clear if it is a pit or not, or another feature.
This locus remains open since it was still visible in the trench.
--  This feature was already discovered in 2004 and L.29 was given by the supervsor. Since the trench is at the E edge of the mound, it lacks with any feature except this one and represent Ubaid fill for the most of its area and the loose ashy soil in the E portion, especially the NE quadrant is representative of the debris from later periods.

label: Locus 8
description: Fill of tannur including and below cobbles and pottery separating it from locus 6.  Associated with outside surface of locus 10.  Second layer of tannur full.  Locus 6 ended at layer of cobbles and pottery.  Locus 8 was these cobbles and below.  Darker and more ashy.  Some burnt and cracked rocks and pottery.

label: Locus 80
description: gray color. fill? some flat lying sherds. harder soil than L75. a little mudbrick debris scattered in the area. visible in the L45 southeast wall  by a dark black line, but not distinct as a surface when exposed.

label: Locus 2070
description: hard packed pinkish brown surface at south baulk

label: Locus 7003
description: This locus is 30 cm. below the surface and is the debris fill located in the 2x2 m sounding in the NE corner.  There are large, flat lying pottery sherds, bones and rocks.  It was debris above the burial, the surface, and another layer of fill dirt.

label: Locus 1087
description: fill underneath the first layer of cobbles and on top of the 2nd layer of cobbles L1086.  No artifacts associated with this fill, although it did go down about 10 cm before we decided to change loci after hitting the cobbles.

label: Locus 7183
description: Mud brick feature located in the southeast corner of the trench. Composed of at least four rows and three courses of brick. The top course is composed of two burnt mud bricks along the western edge of the feature with a yellow unburnt mud brick on both the north and south ends. The two lower courses are also composed of unburnt yellow bricks.  Clear gray or white mortar lines are present. Entire feature is not visible as it runs into the eastern baulk. Continues into trench F2 as locus 2029. Eastern baulk was removed above this feature in order to excavate burial 7221 which cuts into this feature. Although burial 7221 was removed, the bricks were left in situ at the end of the 2005 season.

label: Locus 7004
description: This locus is a burial paralleling the east baulk in A7.  It is within L. 7001 stratum.  It lies within a "step" of dirt which has been cleared on 3 sides.  Head is on south side.

label: Locus 8007
description: THIS IS A GENERAL FILL LOCUS WITH  THE EXCEPTION THAT IT CONTAINS MANY WHITE PEBBLES THROUGHOUT FILL THAT HAS A GOOD CONCENTRATION OF WHITE PEBBLES WHOSE COLOR IS 2.5 Y 8/1 WHITE

label: Locus 5073
description: Mudbrick wall associated with surface L5066.  Fragmentary, possibly due to an unexcavated pit.  Plaster-lined on N face.  Unexcavated.

label: Locus 1003
description: The rock garden. A bunch of medium to large rocks mixed with small rocks and sherds is clumped together 10cm below the surface. There are a bunch of medium sized rocks on the top of this locus, with much the same style of dirt as any of the other loci before this.

label: Locus 2074
description: Removal of fill below mudbrick 2071 to reveal surface 2089.  It has two consistencies mixed, ashy and denser. Has slick troweling consistency buut then becomes ashy and powdery when crushed in hand.

label: Locus 4055
description: this locus number was skipped by mistake.  this locus does not exist.

label: Locus 11
description: Line of stones, what could be possibly the foundation of the wall. It is located in E1 sounding.

label: Locus 2032
description: Area of mudbrick collapse/fill located in southern-most part of trench. Equivalent to L2025 and L2026. Underlying mudbrick walls L2006 and L2020. Abuts L2010. hard as heck. Equals L2025, 2026

label: Locus 5
description: This locus is fill across the entire southern 2/3 of the trench. We changed from L3 to L5 because we noted a change from subtopsoil to eroded layers of occupational debris. mostly compact with some soft areas;

There is a trench that the east half of the locus contains more soft ash and the west half contains more compacted fill. Yet the fill was so soft that we dug half of the locus with a shovel, no picks needed.  We came down on some hard packed fill and switched to L26 because we believed we were at the bottom of the pit. this fill is very mixed between areas of very soft ashy fill and more compact clumps of ashy fill mixed with white shreds of organic material, lots of bones, carbon, pottery etc.

The ground is not very hard for digging which may indicate that it has been left unused for only a few years, regardless of earlier observation. On July 11th we began expanding the trench West 1.5 meters to give us more room in which to look the walls. On July 17th we again expanded North 2 meters from the existing Locus 12. Locus section profile shows 4 subdivisions within the pit: a thicker brown layer just below the plaster of 7219, a relatively thin pale brown/green layer, a distinct dark brown/black ash layer and finally a brown subash layer that ends at the bottom of the pit. subangular sand matrix that is poorly sorted

label: Locus 4019
description: Locus 4019 represents the last of the topsoil and subtopsoil. Skeleton loci numbers not yet assigned (unexcavated).

label: Locus 3004
description: (Previously Level 1) Create 2m x 2m sounding to see the profile and stratigraphic information. This area is heavily disturbed, probably from the washed layers of soil.

label: Locus 2129

hard to the NE and softer with small pebbles and a few flat lying sherds to the SW, ash lens in the center of the southeastern half, ash pit L105 in the eastern corner, mixed EB and Ubaid fill, not good context - very mixed fill and cut by pit L105
*KT dates reflect reorganization

label: Locus 1074
description: fill next to N baulk as we work our way towards the wall 1073.  Same general fill locus as the rest of the trench. label: Locus 126
description:

label: Locus 1
description: This is the opening locus, it exhibits plowing marks of some age, my guess is that field has been left fallow for 10 or more years. There was very little pottery observed as excavation has progressed. No collection of materials is being done for top 0.30 meters. We wanted to open this far west portion of the trench to space our research over a wider part of area F. The top surface is covered with thistles like weeds and small bushy plants that perforate the surface with their long roots. This vegetation was cleared from on top of the trench before excavation began. We then proceeded with large picks, shovels, and wheelbarrows to crack open the surface. General fill mix with debris. Soil is soft facilitating ecavation.

label: Locus 38
description: L38 is poorly preserved mudbrick wall.  We orginally saw it as a clear line of red fill then cut along side it to reveal a layer of melted mudbrick running thru the center of the trench abutting the surface but about 10cm above the surface L37.  We later extended the locus to the west baulk to encompass the cobbles with red melted bricks beneath in L33.  We cleared off what we could see of the red brick wall and changed locus to L41 as the fill directly below the wall.  I thought that the cobble wall in L39 was related to this wall which is a little lower in elevation but the same color brick and the same kind of cobbles so we extended L41 to encompass the fill beneath both walls. this is a poorly preserved mudbrick wall that has no discernable brick lines

label: Locus 9
description: Layer seems to represent a continuation from the previous level. Fill contains occupational debris, potentially undisturbed. Pottery and stone inclusions not scattered evenly throughout

label: Locus 5011
description: Fill covering most of the base of former trench D1.  Appears to be collapsed mudbrick, possibly from higher portions of mudbrick wall features L5008, 5004 or 5012.  Seals surface level L5027 entirely.

label: Locus 119
description: Locus 119 is a fill locus with mixed Middle Bronze and Ubaid artifacts in the southeast corner of the trench. It probably represents some sort of erosion or building phase associated wtih the 2nd millennium street.

label: Locus 6011
description: There was a small layer of mudbrick with bone just beneath it and ash directly to the east against the north baulk.  The bones may be human, but since we were digging the trench as a sounding we were excavating the loci quickly.  Thus, we disturbed the burial before we were able to look at the bones diagnostically. There was mudbrick and ash mixed in small pockets towards the North baulk

label: Locus 1001
description: We changed locus due to a change in the soil color, it seemed to lighten. Later investigations revealed that the soil was the same as the topsoil, it was just harder packed. As the trench the soil appears to be light gray color, but when sprayed it looks exactly like the top soil. We dug about 10cm, finding the same assortment of pottery and bones as the previous layer. We also found that the roots continued into this layer from L.1000. This and a few cobbles, was mapped on our day plan. The stones does not form architecture. The slight change in color from L1000 is due to the sun baking and the burning of organic material (grasses).

label: Locus 3000

There is some flat lying pottery but overall it is probably subtopsoil

The surface was consistent from the middle of the locus to the southeastern corner of the trench, but was patchy from the middle of the locus to the northwest corner of the trench.

label: Locus 1000
description: L1000 is top soil with a few large roots, pebbles and a lot of organic material.  The dark color is probably due to frequent grass burning or the soil baking in the sun.  Also there seems to have been a lot of plowing on the surface. dark color may be due to frequent grass burning, soil baking in the sun, organic material or excessive plowing

label: Locus 159
description: This locus is located at the south end of the trench, bordering the west baulk. It is a white lined pit full of dirt mixed with organic matterial. It is believed that the locus represents a lithic work area that was sealed by the creation of an oven or the burning of the above surface.

description:
This is a wall or a wall base.  The northern edge ends at locus 1068 where burnt dirt and carbon begins.
On 7/14/02 this locus was divided into three loci.  L1069 is the southern section that had the five visible courses and seems to run at a slightly oblique angle from the south to the northeast.  L1075 is the northern section that is mainly one course of flat lying cobbles and pottery with the two flagstones possibly demarking an entrance as well as being the area where a large piece of slag was found.  L1077 is the section between these other two loci of large boulders that do not seem to follow either of the patterns of the other two loci.
KT1069.12 and KT 1073.7 are two halves of the same broken stone bowl.  The bowl halves were inverted and used as wall cobbles for two different walls in my trench.  On 7/14/2 this was split into three loci (1075 and 1077 as well).
This wall had five coures.  Their removal is described in detail in the daily journal.  The top course was of smooth river cobbles placed into the wall at an approximatley 45 degree angle.  The second course was of more of a mud matrix with pebbles.  The third and fourth courses were medium sized cobbles and the final course, the fifth, was of large cobbles and boulders.  There were also a few very flat and thin cobbles placed in this course in the southern baulk.

As 5174 was excavated a rounded and compacted mudbrick feature was identified during trowelling (5200) and a wall line running from the western side of the northern baulk to the northern section of the eastern baulk. By the conclusion of the season the ashy layer identified in bauk section and in plan occupied the north eastern portion of this locus in a triangular area about 0.7 x 0.5 x 0.5 m.

label: Locus 7151
description: Fill located in the southeast quadrant of trench along the east and south baulks. Serves as an "outside" context to wall 7158. rounded, sorted silty clay

label: Locus 7231
description: Ash pit/lens in southeast corner of trench. Relatively shallow with no material culture recovered.

label: Locus 156
description: It is a plaster surface on NW corner of the trench.

label: Locus 30
description: This locus is fill associated with L23. There is an are of ash in the SW corner of the locus.

label: Locus 18
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V
description: The locus is in the west part of the trench

label: Locus 1
description: This locus is topsoil across the entire trench.  note that the steep W-E upwards slope makes the elevations seem really wacky. Not a very thick layer, indicating that there is not much wash accumulation on the western part of the tell in this area.

label: Locus 1004
description: In this area we found a mud brick structure, about 10 cm in width, depth is still unknown, it continue to next level (locus 1009).  This area is mainly composed of hard compacted, mud-brick like layer.  Especially around the NW corner is compacted and white in color compared to other area.

label: Locus 4024
description: This locus is a pit, and it is round shape and at the bottom I hit a hard material, I thought that I came to bottom but I am not at the bottom right now.But, the shape of the pit is not a complete round, it is mostly like a conical.

label: Locus 4021
description: It is the contution of the floor of L4020. But, it is unsealed on the other hand it equals L4020.

label: Locus 2
description: It is not clear if this is a wall. There is just one visable big stone at the west edge of L2 and a lot of shards (predominantly coarse)

label: Locus 4014
description: This is a cobble wall found over a week ago and left pedastelled until we found out if these cobbles are associated with the ones in the eastern half of the trench.  This locus was extended when we found additional cobbles extending the second course of stones to the south baulk.  So this locus is the removal locus for the wall, the fill above the extention of the second course of the wall and the second course stones (about 1m long) that were left in situ.  The wall itself was 2 courses and 1 row but was probably wider judging from the continuation of the bottom course which was about 4 rows wide. The soil is brittle and dry but gets continually softer and more moist as you descend down.

label: Locus 4
description: this is most likely a tumble or colapse. this may also be the result of erosion. under the large rocks there was a mud brick layer. the mud bricks were not defined into into individual bricks. there was also a large deposite of fine white clay that ran back into the balk. piled rocks of differing types. large porus white 10 YR 8/1. smoth rounded 2.5 10 bg. mud brick surface underneath the rocks. no defined bricks.

label: Locus 1008
description: The locus is not revealing any cultural material.  At this point Bradley and Andy both agreed to close the trench. The small rocks remain consistent in size with previous loci @ 5cm X 5cm

label: Locus 17
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V

label: Locus 4019
description: The fill in the NW 1/4 of the trench between the loci:  4018, 4017, 4025, 4023, 4022. Just an arbitrary division because i did not want to continiue with the sub top soil locus where I startd to find out different features.

label: Locus 137
description:
This locus is located against the eastern baulk of D8 south of the walls in Locus 135. It probably represents a wall collapse. 
The size of this locus has changed since new locus was designated out of this area (new locus L138). Current dimensions are 2.4m x 1.10m and its shape is irregular (see plan).

label: Locus 4035
description:
L4035 is a layer of fill resting under 4031, 4032, and 4030.  It also extends laterally and is cut by 4029 and possibly 4034 and 4033.  Contains an pot drop (shown on sketch map).

Current idea is to consider a baseline locus of fill throughout the trench starting at about this level.  All other loci will be identified because they are distinct from this general fill.

label: Locus 5195
description: section taken from pit 5180, floor 5194 and fill locus 5190 to assess any stratigraphy in the southeast corner of the trench before further excavation. The fill continues in the vertical level of the section with no clear stratigraphy.

label: Locus 13
description: Ubaid fill beneath the Pit L.11.

label: Locus 33
description: L33 is a row of 6 stones in the south of our 2nd step.It consists of six large stones found very near the surface.It cappears to have suftural much from erosion.

label: Locus 13
description: Very hard surface.  Possibly associated iwth pebble foundation of locus 11.  Different texture and hardness than rest of locus 10.  So taken separately.

label: Locus 182
description: Locus 182 is a stone wall below Locus 170 in the eastern baulk extension of the trench. It appears to be above the stones uncovered in Locus 178 on the 27th, and borders mudbrick wall Locus 181.

label: Locus 5
description: topsoil. a 1.5m wide swath following the slope of the trench and the line of L1. top soil

label: Locus 5038
description: Deposit of sand and clay apparently built up against wall L5039 and in the area S of there.  Not  a very thick layer, but possibly indicative of a period of disuse.  Has a slight downward slope to the E.

label: Locus 36
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V
description: I t is pebble surface on SE corner of the trench.

label: Locus 148
description: This locus is located south of L146, at the center-east part of the trench and its east border is the East trench baulk.  It yields large amount of ground stone, fragments of ground stone, stone implements, and cores. fill with ground stone tools scattered on the surface at the opening elevation. Some ceramic sherds present and river rocks present also.

label: Locus 1095
description: This began as an arbitrary locus division to go down in an area which appeared different than the surface 1089.  Was originally 1.5 x 1.5.  But after looking at the soil we realized that this area along the S baulk and going out for awhile was actually much different than the hard baked clay surface over on the N side of the trench.

label: Locus 1128
description: Fill below mud brick wall/feature L1110 in southeast corner of trench extending west out from the east baulk. Abuts with wall L1123 on its west end.

label: Locus 7174
description: Mud plaster surface in the northwest corner of the trench superimposed below surface 7168. Excavated using the Household Archaeology Protocol (HAP). Found to also be bonded with mud brick wall 7163. 24 total liters

label: Locus 132
description: This locus is fill, covering 4.5m north of the suthern edge of trench D8.  It abuts  L132 (to the north) and the area east which has no assigned locus number yet. In notes, L132 is referred to as a "courtyard" area. courtyard area south of house structure. on the closing level, areas of ashy dirt and a single orange-brown stain visible.

label: Locus 5
description: Thin layer of light clayish soil. I would say that it was blown in by wind over time before it solidified or was covered by vegetation. Thin, wind blown dust layer

label: Locus 4
description: Fill on the western side of the wall is being kept as a different locus to maintain good control and identified possible differences or even likenesses in material from either side general fill

label: Locus 4042
description: This area of the E side of the trench equals with L4041, but it is not sealed. It has a few ceramic pieces laying on.

label: Locus 4045
description: the fill under the L4021. Kind of same with L4021 but it has a different strata coming out so I changed the locus arbitrarily. soft dirt between features

label: Locus 1003
description: L1003 is fill above a rock surface.  We changed locus from L1002 because the soil became lighter and harder packed.  There were scattered pebbles in the soil and some roots, not very much pottery and lots of small white flecks that may be plaster/limestone.  When we saw the cobble surface we leveled the trench and changed locus. much lighter than previous locus and harder as well

label: Locus 31
description:
Surface  - pebbles in a soil matrix - pebbles up to 1.5 cm with an occasional 4 cm stone.  Also exists in D5 as L5194 - Ubaid date?
Locus continues at end of 2004 season.

label: Locus 29
description:
This is the fill inside the pit bordered by L20, 5 and 6.
Locus 29 extends to the East of furnace L2/L20 directly in front of the 5 chambers. We created this locus to isolate this material for sampling and diagnosis. We have been excavating 2 cm at a time, sampling 100% of soil. We have found very few artifacts here.

label: Locus 1
description:
Topsoil-

7/03- 1st step: Consistent greyish earth with much pottery and some animal bone and lithics. We began excavation in the NW corner and followed the slope of the tepe. At .7m we noticed a reddish color shift and came down on oven L2. We also found slag (L1KT4) near oven L2.

7/04- 2nd step (east of 1st): composition and strategy same as 1st step.  Oven L5 found near the surface. loose soil with much pottery and small roots

label: Locus 7185
description: Plaster surface layer below 7182 in the northwest corner of the trench. Bonded with walls 7154 and 7163. Heavy burning and ashy deposits on the eastern end of the locus. Excavated using the Household Archaeology Protocol (HAP). HAP sample taken from the western end of the locus directly below the HAP sample from L7182. The total surface measured as 54 liters. 54 total liters

label: Locus 8
period_label: Early Bronze Age I / Late Chalcolithic V
description: The locus is East of the trench and under the locus 6.

label: Locus 2128
description: This locus is a pit, located by the southern end of the Eastern baulk. I believe, and hope, that we caught the top of the pit. It is possible that it is layered, because of the difference in soil types in the pit.

label: Locus 32
description: L32 is the extremely dense material to the west of wall L16.

label: Locus 4026
description: Removed contaminated topsoil and subdivided the area underneath it for better control over the areas in the trench. Much the same soil as L4025 and L 4029.

label: Locus 3
description: 25 cm arbitrary level through E part of the trench - contains topsoil

label: Locus 2105
description: subsurface fill located directly below area where basket impression L2085 was removed; equivalent to fill 2111 below plaster surface 2106 in area between the 4m-5m pegs.

label: Locus 4003
description: This locus is fill on top of and east of a large cobble surface/collapse area.  We started the locus by articulating a line of stone extending NE to SW.  These stones became the top of an extended cobble surface and L4003 became all of the fill east of the cobble surface.  We peeled back slowly looking for surfaces associated with the cobbles but did not find anything.  The soil remained the same color.  The south edge of this locus has changed many times and mixed with the North edge of L4004 on several ocassions because the fill is identical. This fill is topsoil above a cobble stone wall and assocated surface.  Large cobbles run single file NE to SW down the tepe and are .10m to .20m wide.  There are large pieces of pottery found in situ near the cobbles.   A few chunks of conglomerate rock w

label: Locus 4
description: General continuation of the fill from L1, dug as an arbitrary level. orange brown splotches continue throughout (7.5YR 6/6)

label: Locus 5170
description: feature identified as a wall by its compactness against the layer material of locus 5169. only a very thin sliver of the wall was left implying that it had been levelled, perhaps in the building of the 2002 Ubaid house.

label: Locus 34
description: This fill is located south of wall 33. It was perceived that the wall did not extend into the southern baulk, and locus 34 was excavated down to the first stones of the wall visible in the southern baulk, which appear lower down than to the north. In a sesne it is not distinct from debris fill loci 37, 35, and 36.

label: Locus 4000
description: L4000 was formerly part of L4021 (Level 8) when the trench was a section called F4.  The locus was started because we found a complete pot (SF KT#4027) on a mound of hard burnt clay, apparently in situ in undisturbed context.  There was some loose fine grained slit still in the pot so we took a sample (KT 4028).  The rest of the surface is far from level and is made of very hard clay/mudbrick like material.  We closed the locus when we found a large collection of what looked like surface material, bones, pottery and a few small finds found flat on the floor an almost complete pot was found atop some burnt clay and ash.  No pit or surface was found but the strata indicates that we are under a surface.  The present layer must have been closed by a layer of tightly compacted clayey silt.

label: Locus 3
description: Removal of subsoil.  Search for good contexts

label: Locus 2051
description: mudbrick collapse located in the southern part of trench; deposited by a collapsed mudbrick wall (possibly from L2056 or L2042/2066).

label: Locus 2121
description: fill with rock band (L2122) running thru it; located at 12-13.5m pegs

label: Locus 7
description: The locus is West part of the trench. It is coming under locus 5. continue subsoil

label: Locus 1101
description: This is the possible mudbrick surface running along the western baulk.  A mudbrick in this area was exposed in cross-section in pit 1091.

label: Locus 4069
description: This locus is a very soft. First we though that it might be a floor but after starting to excavate the locus we have seen that the rocks and stones that are in this locus are only collapse ones.This locus is below the fill layer from last year that had the locus number as 4034.

label: Locus 41
description: This locus lies below locus 23 and was distinguished from the overlying locus 23 because of the mud brick debris to the north and the emergence of new fill loci numbers to the south as a result of the stone wall 33. Otherwise it is not different from the overlying locus 23, a fine brown fill shaped like a narrow channel running east to west.

label: Locus 5054
description: Fill in central area of trench.  Mostly loose soil with some areas of ash and sand/silt.  Appears to be a between-phase layer between the L5027/L5034 occupation and L5066 occupation.  Closed at end of season, still sealing some parts of L5066.

label: Locus 117
description: Locus 117 is a mudbrick wall emerging out of the west baulk near the center of the the trench.  No bricks were discernable in the removal of the locus suggesting that the locus represents mud brick slump or a highly weathered wall.

label: Locus 40
description: This is a fill beloww very active L25

label: Locus 24
description: There are no KT bags from this locus. But the dirt was very hard and tightly packed with little rocks and a bunch of potsherds.

label: Locus 2006
description: L 2006 is an area of large stones uncovered while digging L 2005. It was closed when the level of the soil change from 8/8/2000 was reached.

label: Locus 88
description: fill underlying flat sherd surfaces (?) or just a continuation of fill level

label: Locus 7104
description: This is the human burial which was going to be taken out by the bone people two years ago. We are starting to take it out of it`s place.

label: Locus 123
description: Locus 123 is a fill locus in the southwest corner of the trench abutting a possible emerging wall in Locus 126. It probably represents a midden of some sorts given the high concentrations of pottery, lithics and animal bones.

label: Locus 7172
description: Subsurface fill in southeastern corner of the trench. Tightly packed clay with residual river pebbles. poorly sorted, sandy matrix, tightly packed/hard

label: Locus 4118
description: This wall runs NE to SW on the West side of the trench. It is currently associated with the wall L4116 and floor L4115.

label: Locus 5175
description: Well defined single mudbrick distinguished by colour difference with 5163.

label: Locus 1005
description: Under the pot smashes of 1004, and the rock garden of 1003, we found some more mixed up sand with white specs.  We use this locus to define the dirt removed as we leveled this possible surface. White specs and some red spots mixed with the otherwise 1002-like dirt.

label: Locus 2130
description: Reed mat used as structural support; this mat runs in between courses of mudbrick in L2126 and into 2125 ; reeds showed possible burn or excess decay evidence at the southern and western extremities. Same material as another reed mat 2141 which runs between courses of stones in 2139--stone footing for mudbrick wall system; also same material as L2145 reed mat running between mudbrick layers at the south edge of 2139. white reed impression at east baulk and adjacent to 2126, but burned/charred at south and west portions of preserved mat.

label: Locus 1000
description: Topsoil.

label: Locus 4001
description: sub-top soil. Between the exposed topsoil and as the rock gardens scatered all about the trench, we have this locus as a simple dirt fill. It continiued as artificial baulks for a lon time, cutting the trench into quarters. softer than the L4000, but still dry and crumbly

label: Locus 101
description: This is a set of floors (aat least 2) inside a roomm. Most of this area was blown out by a roomm i nthe later house so only a small portion of these surfaces were preserved.

label: Locus 3027
description: This is a broken cobble surface that is associated with ovens 3030 and 3003. This surface is brolen in several places and in the west is undefinable

label: Locus 2119
description: This locus contains the removal of the last part of wall L2116. The very northern part in this particular case.

label: Locus 55
description: This locus is a rock wall, possibly the foundation for wall L17 (same as L51)

label: Locus 2152
description: This locus describes the removal of a heap of stones, the heap was triangular in shape,sticking out from the south baulk, running along the now removed wall L2117, on the south side of the wall.

label: Locus 2025
description: Area east of the mudbricks 2023.  Designated as a separate locus due to the presence of the wall stub/collapse L2023.  Only fill.  No surface found, although it was cut by a pit L-2024.  The locus was closed when the wall stub was removed.  It was then recombined with L-2025, the same material into L-2037.

label: Locus 5042
description: Fill below rock-jumble ridden fill locus 5020.  Possibly some areas are still topsoil contaminated, especially in the NE.  Closed due to end of season.

label: Locus 1002
description: Begin this locus because I found some soil variation and there were possible pits (this turned out not to be pits).  The possible wall ended in this level.  Found no feature or cultural level.  this locus is sub-topsoil and seem to be somewhat disturbed.  I closed this Locus because we reached the finishing elevation of the locus 1000.  Now I made the entire trench leveled.

label: Locus 4016
description: There are a few ceramic pieces from the Ubaid period.

label: Locus 2025
description: Mix of soils in the N part of the trench - difficult to differentiate particular areas to isolate; ashy, mudbrick mix

label: Locus 2004
description: L2004 is the southern 3/5 of the trench.  It is characterized by a medium packed, grayish brown soil.

label: Locus 2123
description: "Plaster" topped pit in L2122 (from 2001) near west baulk was L2078. This pit had a sort of bowl shaped crust of pottery and plaster ? In it and underneath were potsherds aligned with the side of the pit lining the pit irregulary near the top 5-10 cm. Below this there was a mass of potsherds of very small size totally mixed with highly fired dirt so that it was hard to seperate the sherds ( and a few oven fragments) from the soil. For purpose of soil sample is a Thermal pit.

label: Locus 2024
description: L2024 is a surface to the north of L2014. It was so designated because of large potsherds and stones atop it.

label: Locus 1006
description: L1006 is a cobble pebble surface. Measuring from the east to west baulk. The surface is devoid of cultural debris, leading one to think this may  be a result of slope wash on a gulley.  The stones are definitely in a pattern and seem to be straightly placed by nature.  The average size of the cobbles is about 8-10cm w/ some pebbles strewn throughout.

label: Locus 11
description: This locus is the area directly bellow L7. It was changed to help preserve context for L9, the floor. the soil was much more densly packed and harder to pick through here, once it was out and the soil dried it was a very fine sand texture.

label: Locus 2
description: subtopsoil

label: Locus 12
description: LEVEL OF ROCK AND POTSHERDS THAT WAS REACHED AS THE PREVIOUS LOCUS WAS BEING REMOVED. WE TOOK GREAT CARE IN OBTAINING THE EDGES OF IT. WE WILL COLLECT THOSE MATERIALS DISPLACED DURING ARTICULATION AND CLEANING. FOR PURPOSES OF DIAGNOSTICS THESE MATERIALS COUL BE CONSIDERED THE SAME AS LOCUS 14 MIXED MATERIALS RESTING ON THE SURFACE

label: Locus 158
description: Locus 158 is a fill Locus encompassing the entire trench. It is characterized by a uniform soil texture and composition and is cut by thr remnants of pit Locus 157.

label: Locus 7170
description: Plastered floor located in the northwest corner of the trench. Bonded to walls 7154 and 7163. Cut on the south end by pit 7162. Sealed by debris and ash from 7161. Two 18-20 cm long burnt mud bricks (debris) are sitting on and slightly cutting into the floor. Excavated using the Household Archaeology Protocol (HAP). Due to high compaction, a soil sample was not able to be collected. The surface totalled 35 liters.

label: Locus 39
description: CANCELED! this locus was cancled and combined with L36 to make L44. This was done because both these loci were refering to the same wall.

label: Locus 2057
description: Bricky layer south of 2050

label: Locus 5046
description: Rock garden.  Large (up to 40cm) rock in no apparent organization.  May be some sort of foundation for wall L5037, though it seems unlikely, or tumble from upslope.  Closed at end of season.

label: Locus 7092
description: THIS IS NOT AN ACTUAL LOCUS...I SKIPPED THE LOCUS # BY ACCIDENT.

label: Locus 5009
description: Section/sounding through mudbrick wall L5008, which seems to show the wall may only have a single course.  Area below is a surface level with a possible oven.  Actually did not cut wall but came to its edge.

label: Locus 4010
description: This locus is fill east of the surface collapse in L4004 and a curved wall in L4019.  THis fill is also abov the rock wall in L4019 and abuts th wall on its east side.  We dug down to find surfaces to associate the architecture but found nothing.  When we reached the end of the topsoil we found a huge area of soft ashy soil that may be a pit and changed locus. This fill has very little cultural material.  We dug mostly through topsoil then found some soft ashy type soil at the bottom

label: Locus 10008
description: New arbirary locus

label: Locus 2008
description: 2008 is a fill layer on the se quad of the trench.  It exists so that we may keep horizontal control over what seems to be a very large fill layer (2007+2008+2009+2010). possibly the same stratigraphic layer as 2007, 2009, and 2010.

label: Locus 150
description: Locus 150 is an Ubaid fill locus on the east side of wall 131, running to the east baulk of the trench.

label: Locus 8023
description: Completely round pit dug through at least 2 levels. It is almost perfectly circular and my guess is that it was originally used for storage and later for cooking as there was little evidence of heavy burning or cooking remains closer to surface some bone and ash mixed with soil was observed. All contents were removed and sifted. No plaster lining was seen on walls or floors. It would appear by how shallow it was that it was not used very long darker soil within pit

label: Locus 14
description: Wall found within the N baulk. It may have more than one wall. One is N wall of room L.7 and the other may be built on top of it later.

label: Locus 4045
description: This is the area beneath 4044.  The soil is exactly the same as the soil for L4042.  the locus is different because we removed the rocks afterwards.

label: Locus 2107
description: This locus is removal of fill below that of L2103 which was the subfloor of L2096 that was excavated in 2001. It is equal to L2109, because of the lack of difference in almost all aspects (color, texture and soforth). lenses of mudbrick debris, charcoal, clay, gravel

label: Locus 73
description: It is a building (or room) with big rocks.

label: Locus 5
description: An area without a pit like shape, that may have been an intentional dump outside of the wall or maybe just a low spot on the terrain. No ash or trash was observed. Soil was loose and several small cobblestones were observed on top of fill. This was removed with contents once removed showing a fairly shallow pit On the surface of what appears and feels like a pit there are several small stones and very soft soil with no compaction. No ash is evident despite the grayish color of the fill.

label: Locus 4017
description: It is the floor, under the surface that I was trying to reach

label: Locus 8032
description: Area NW of wall 8034

label: Locus 5217
description: This is new locus number opened when the L.5206 is closed. Even though the soil texture and color was very similar to L.5206, a new locus was necessary because plaster surface L. 5216 was discovered in the E of L.5206. In addition, the tumbled down ground stone found near the plaster surface indicates that we may be getting into a new deposit. If there will be no significant change in the soil character, then it might be concluded in the end that this locus and L. 5206 are the same.

label: Locus 5117
description: Fill in cental-W portion of trench and below the rock group, L5099, above grain surface L5098 or the earthen surface after the former has gone to its full extent.

label: Locus 4011
description: Rocks in the NE portion of the trench close to the E baulk with a high rock at the E side. There is some yellowish sand stone under  the pile. Also two of the  big rocks were kind of flat. This locus was sitting on top of the corner of the walls L4030 and 4041. a high vertical stone at the E side of the locus

label: Locus 44
description:
L44 is the fill between the walls of L14 and L20. It is comprised of fill and debris.This chamber seems to be linked to mayn chamber  / furnace,
in that it shaves a wall (i.c. the south wall of the major structure L20) and the back wall (the N-S  wall) seemed to have been bonded to the furnace"s  E-W  wall. Fill inside S chamber 14.

label: Locus 23
description: This locus consists of the brown, fine fill dirt north of locus 17. Originally it was thought that this locus was the interior of an installation bounded by mud brick in the east (locus 24). However, excavation of the locus found no artifacts or any other data to confirm the existence of the installation. Hence, this locus is restricted to a fill type described above. It consistently preserves the same colour and consistency throughout its depth apart from occasional mud brick debris against the western section, and is distinguished from the surrounding loci 17, 26, 27, and 28. Occasionally metal slag was encountered. However this is also true of loci 17 and 28.

label: Locus 83
description: fill inside walls 70, 72 and 71

label: Locus 21
description: THIS IS THE THIRD SUCCESSIVE WHITE ORGANIC SURFACE AFTER LOCI 12 AND 14 ALL OF WHICH ARE SEPARATED BY SEMI-COMPACT TO COMPACT FILLS AND SEEM TO UNDERLIE WALL COLLAPSE. LOCUS 21 HOWEVER CONTAINS SOME FLAT-LYING SHERDS AND THE REED IMPRESSIONS ARE MUCH MORE SUBSTANTIAL THAN THE OTHER SURFACES. FURTHERMORE THIS LOCUS IS CLEARLY BOUNDED IN THE FORM OF A RECTANGLE, BEYOND WHICH THE SHITE SURFACE DOES NOT EXTEND. AND THE SURFACE SLOPES DRAMATICALLY FROM SOUTH TO NORTH IN THE DIRECTION OF LOCUS 17. This locus was excavated by removing the impressions entirely in chunks and transporting them in shoeboxes. After excavations of the trench were completed it became clear that white organic deposits are to be associated with the wet course construction of mud brick walls.

label: Locus 50
description:
L50 is the mudbrick collapse directly below L27 and L20 in the NW quadrant. It eguals L29 and is collapse of the same jumbled of fill and mudbrick.
The northern 1/3 was left unexcavated in case any further guestions about the foundations of L20 arise. The curent theory is that is the debri of previous furnaces.

label: Locus 9024
description: It rained the night before so the hard clay texture might just be because of that.

label: Locus 117
description: pebbly pit. cut L116. possibly extends farther south into L110 and L120, but this section of the pit was not well preserved due to mixing. very loose soil

label: Locus 48
description: This locus is a cleaning locus. It was created to help flatten and level the area between the south edge of L30 and the north edge of L17.

label: Locus 4002
description: L4002 is fill that abuts L4001 and L4003.  Made of hardpacked clay that comes off in jagged pieces.  We began to uncover a surface near the north east baulk so we changed locus to L4004. This is soil exactly the same as in section F5 when its is picked is comes off in jagged pieces.

label: Locus 4005
description: L4005 is the north baulk of trench B1.  We cut about .24m off the baulk to see the stratigraphy better and to get an idea of what we would encounter in the adjacent trench. the color varies as you continue down the wall.  There are pits and surfaces and mudbrick walls in section

label: Locus 2060
description: Couple remaining somewhat coherent brickey pieces removed above stones of wall. mudbrick pieces, erosiaonal mixed soil above stones

label: Locus 2004
description: L2004 is the fill directly below L2001 on the western half of the trench. These two loci are probably the same stratigraphic layer. We changed them due to the architecture found on the eastern half of the trench so as to not mix artifacts from the architecture with those of the fill.

label: Locus 5140

label: Locus 162
description: This locus is fill located in the northwest corner of the trench. It touches the walls of L157 and is outside the Ubaid house. We believe that at least half of this locus is a part of L156 becasue the soil is the same. It has traces of the same surface present in L164 and the color and texture of the soil is the same as L156. It is its own locus because it did not present the same traces of surface that were present in L156, L164, L166, or L168.  Either it is different, or its preservation of the relevant material is bad.  As stated above it has similar soil and context to these loci, and thus is thought to be at least contemporary.  To dig it we have gone down to the same level as the abutting surfaces, keeping them roughly together in depth so as to notice any relevant differences between the two.  About 35cm down we discovered that there were multiple mudbricks on the ground.  Looking at the baulk, these mudbricks continue up into the baulk for about 30cm with 4 courses that we can see.  Obviously we cut through them and didn"t see them until now.  Additionally about 20cm north of these bricks is an incomplete line of stones.

label: Locus 7221
description: Interior rectangular burial pit cutting into platform 7183 in the southeast corner of the trench. Pit is lined on all sides by burnt and unburnt mud bricks of L7183, which is three courses deep. Soft brown silty matrix with some pebbles below a dried out angular gray matrix toplevel. Ash is present on the upper most levels but not internally. 3-5 possble fire-cracked rocks inside on upper most elevations. Human burial is composed of an adult male, based on size of the pelvis, in a flexed position on the left side running in an east-west orientation. The right leg and foot rest on top of the left leg and foot. The right arm rests on the left forearm. The left hand is near the skull which faces south. Some pottery sherds were recovered near the body but no obvious grave goods. A carbon sample was recovered from the fill just above the hands. Note: burial was only able to excavated after the partial removal of the eastern baulk separating F7 from F2. poorly sorted, angular to rounded, silt matrix

label: Locus 170
description: This locus is the subfloor fill below the surface L169.  L169 was likely one of a series of surfaces pushed together with little or no fill between, and there are still pieces of these surfaces present on the exposed layer of this fill.  Either there is a poorly preserved surface in this fill or the surface above was irregular and not level.  On the northwestern corner of the fill is a particularly large section of surface belonging to the layers above this locus, measuring to about 3ft.  In excavating the locus we left this in place until the rest had gone down about 5cm to make sure it was nothing different, and then took it out as apart of the locus.  There is not a lot of artifacts, rocks, or anything of the sort in this fill.  It had few inclusions and produced small amounts of pottery, lithic, shell, and bone.  Its border with the ashy soil of L167 is fairly undefined, and the ashy runs into this locus quite a bit.

label: Locus 8
description: Cobblestone surface / fill. tightly packed.  Very few artifacts on its surface.  Stones larger to the west, more smaller stones and pebbles towards the eastern edge.  Slopes down significantly north to south, and is thicker to the south, suggesting that this locus served to fill in a depression.  Indeed when we dug below this locus we found wall L11 running E-W, and the cobble fill of L8 is thinnest over the wall and thickest to the south.  So clearly L8 served to fill in/cover over the ruins of wall L11 and fill L12 (south of the wall).  The locus contained very little cultural material, indicating that it was used for a very short period of time, kept very clean, and most likely was not a road or other route that one would expect to receive lots of traffic and accumulate lots of trash.  The absence of cultural material also suggests that the stones were brought from an uncontaminated area like the river bed, rather than scavenged from some location on the site itself, which would likely have contained lots of local garbage.
